"A little too much," Kara grumbles to herself.

Alex sighs and zips the body bag. "Come on," she says, "let's go back upstairs. Is Lena in the med bay ?"

Kara nods. "She's asleep. Doctor Veritas gave her painkillers and a dose of Skelegro for, um, the bones I might have maybe cracked a little when I pushed her." She adds that last part under her breath, sheepish and ashamed.

"You saved her life. And we are not calling it that," Alex says firmly, not for the first time.

"It's a serum that fixes bones, what else do you want to call it ?"

"BGXS-2020, as it was intended."

"You're no fun."

"And I'm also the boss."

"Not yet," Kara reminds her with a laugh, "J'onn is still around."

She goes to mess up her hair but Alex, having anticipated it, jumps out of the way and stalks up the corridor.

"Hey !" Kara catches up with a burst of superspeed. "Wait for me."

Alex rolls her eyes, but still holds the door open for her.

In the med bay, Lena is sleeping soundly ; face relaxed and mouth slightly parted to let out regular puffs of warm breath. There's an angry bruise blooming on her otherwise marble-like cheek. She must have hit her head on the way down. Her left hand is immobilised in a cast, just for the couple of hours it's going to take for her bone to mend itself, and Kara is holding the other in her own, soothing her thumb on her soft skin.

In her other hand, she holds the bullet, turning it over and over between her fingers. It's oblong, hollow point, would have gone straight through her heart without Kara's intervention. She shudders at the thought, pockets it and returns to her silent observation of Lena's sleeping form. Physically, she'll be okay, and it's all Kara can allow herself to think about right now.

She has hurt Lena, again. And sure, this time the dark bruise spreading on her cheek is an indication that she saved her, but she can't help but feel unclean and unworthy of her, like an uncouth bull in a china shop who breaks everything she touches. Her now free hand trembles, and she tucks it under her thigh in an effort to cease the shaking. She forces herself to relax, leaning back in the chair and closing her eyes, but her whole body is still tense and deadly ; somedays, she still hates herself, just a little, just enough.

***

Lena does not wake up for the rest of the night. Naturally, Kara does not go to sleep at all. She remains sitting on the uncomfortable chair, legs sprawled in front of her and free hand still tucked underneath herself. The entire world seems intent on visiting during the hours that stretch endlessly towards the morning. Sam shows up a little after 11pm with a blanket and a box of Lena's favourite tea, Brainy swings by around one with a report on Graves' gun confirming that it's not sold anywhere, and just before three, Nia sticks her head in through the gap in the door to very helpfully state that she, "did not see that one coming," which Kara had figured out on her own. Finally, Alex comes again at five on the dot, smelling freshly of Kelly's rose soap and with her hair still damp from her shower. She drags a three legged stool closer to the bed and plops down on it unceremoniously, a gruff expression etched on her face.

"I took the liberty of getting in touch with Stryker's warden," she says without preamble.

Kara inhales sharply, and holds her breath. She notices that a flap of skin has gotten loose on her prosthetic, but resists the urge to pick at it.

"Were you going to tell me Luthor tried to get in touch with Lena ?"

Kara releases her breath. "She asked me not to," she says.

Alex hums quietly, then, "why ?" she asks.

"I don’t know. I suppose she didn’t want to make a fuss about it."

"That does sound like Lena."

Kara squeezes Lena’s hand, gently, not hard enough to wake her up, but enough to let her know in her sleep that she’s here. "It does," she confirms.

"You did do something about it," Alex continues. It's not a question, but more of a prompt for Kara to keep talking. Alex knows, without needing to be told, that her sister didn't just leave it at that.

Kara sighs, briefly closing her eyes before she opens them again to cast a glance at the barren room. "I asked Nia to keep an eye on Lex."

"And what did she say ?"

"Something big’s coming."

It doesn't take more for Alex. "I'll up security."

"Lena's not going to be happy about that," Kara says, softly trailing her thumb on the back of her girlfriend's hand.

"I’ll up security discreetly," Alex corrects. "Put Brainy on it."

"Already done."

"And he managed to keep me out of the loop ?" Alex asks, her amazement just short of an impressed whistle.

"You know he unhooked himself from the mainframe."

"And thank God for that," Alex grumbles. "One traumatising event is more than enough."

Kara snickers. She wasn't here on that fateful day but she's heard plenty of recounts of Brainy accidentally uploading his porn research on all of the DEO's screens simultaneously. Nia couldn't look at anyone in the eye for an entire week, but apparently the couple's sex life is vibrant.

Her laughter makes Lena stir, but she still doesn't wake up for another two hours. Kara counts as they trickle by slowly on the old digital clock that adorns the wall. It doesn't show the seconds, unlike an antic time piece with hands and a maddening sound ; and she's grateful for it. She thinks it would have driven her crazy. Even if by some accounts, including hers, she is already crazy. It's something she wants to say sometimes, scream even, to the people who think she's just okay. She wants them to know that sometimes, she still hears his voice in her head. She knows he's dead, she made sure of it herself, and no one could have survived what she did ; after all, she technically didn't. But some days, she can't help but check over her shoulder for an unwanted presence, can't help but clamp her hands over her ears at the mere suspicion of a hated sound. Some days, she doesn't even dare to speak, for fear that it's his inflection that will resonate in her words.

Being around Lena makes it better. Lena makes everything better. She's here to be strong when Kara cannot be, to support her when she bends ; and Kara knows that if it weren't for her, she might not even have made it through her first few weeks back on Earth, when everything was so loud and bright all the time, when the rather simple act of breathing was, more often than not, unbearable. Lena centres her, Lena grounds her, and Lena is no longer asleep. Kara snaps out of her dark thoughts to focus on her and states, rather plainly, "you're awake."

Lena groans, and fast as lightning, Kara produces a small glass of cool water for her. The cardboard is a little damp and sticky, but Lena pays it no mind as she gulps it down, some of it trickling down her cheek as she struggles with her splinted hand. "My mandatory quarterly assassination attempt was early this time," she croaks.

Kara has half a mind of letting her know how unfunny this is, but Lena looks morose enough that she doesn't really want to add to it. Instead, she combs her fingers softly through her hair, wiping from her forehead a couple of strands that have gotten loose.

"Can you tell me what happened ? I remember getting on the podium. Then pain. But not much else."

"That was me actually," Kara says, trying to keep her voice even. "Someone tried to shoot you and I may have pushed you aside a little too enthusiastically."

"You saved my life," Lena states, quite simply.

"I." Kara swallows. She can feel the bullet in her pocket, the one she snatched mid-air and that would have most certainly taken the love of her life from her. "Yes, probably."

Lena squeezes her hand, then brings it to her mouth and lays a tender kiss on her palm. "Thank you." She breathes against her for a moment, small puffs of warm air tickling Kara's skin. "Did you stop the shooter ?" she asks eventually. "Was anyone hurt ?"

"He, detonated himself," Kara says, choosing her words carefully. "But I shielded everyone from the blast, and as far as I know, no one was majorly hurt. Apart from my suit."

"Shame," Lena whispers, "I liked that suit." She shakes her head from side to side, smiles a little crookedly. "Did you manage to identify him ?"

"I. Yes," Kara admits, seeing no point in lying but still trying to stave off the inevitable.

"And ?"

"Otis Graves."

Lena's mouth rounds in a little nearly silent "oh." She looks down at her hands, then fixes her gaze somewhere in the distance, looking at something that Kara can't see. "Lex then," she says. "How predictable."

"And yet, we didn't predict it."

"How did he get past security ?" Lena asks. "Alex had dozens of agents on site."

This time, it's Kara who looks down at her hands and she has to concede, "no idea."

Lena frowns, and remains silent for a long moment. "I suppose the DEO will want to get involved with this now ?"

"It sort of already is involved," Kara confesses. "I might have maybe asked Nia and Brainy to keep an eye on you."

Lena squeezes her eyes shut, exhales slowly. "I should have known you wouldn't leave it at that."

She doesn't sound angry, more resigned, but her tone still rests heavily on Kara's stomach.

"Let us protect you," she says, "please."

Lena sighs, and for a second, Kara thinks she's about to refuse. "Fine," she finally says. "But if you have to dig into Luthor business for this, please, talk to me about it. I don't want you to think ill of me for what you could see."

"What Lex did will never change the way I see you," Kara replies, leaning in to lay a kiss at the corner of her mouth. "I promise."

She searches for Lena's gaze, refuses to move until their eyes meet and she sees in them a quiet but fierce determination.

***

"I just don't understand why now ?" Lena says, pacing the floor at an interesting speed for someone who was just cleared of a concussion.

Kara has an inkling as to "why now ?" but she doesn't want to be the one who says it. Because the fact that "why now ?" is because of her is fairly easy to deduce, and she can't possibly be the only one who has come to this conclusion. After all, Lex Luthor didn't hesitate to mutilate an entire city to get to Superman, offing his own sister for her association to Supergirl doesn't seem too out of the realm of possibilities.

President Marsdin seems to agree with her. Or at least that's how Kara interprets her hawk-like gaze and her reinforced security detail. Lex Luthor just declared war on Supergirl from his clearly not secured enough prison cell and everyone who's close to her is at risk now.

"Whatever it is," Alex says, stopping Lena's wild course by putting a gentle but firm hand on her shoulder, "we'll find it, and we'll put a stop to it."

Lena sighs, opens her mouth to fire back, her anxiety brimming on the tip of her tongue, but President Marsdin cuts her off. "I have already given the order to increase security around your brother, Miss Luthor," she says, her lilt regal and composed. "He will temporarily be moved to a highly secured and undisclosed location while we dismantle the rest of his network. The DEO will have free range for this and in the meantime, I ask that you report directly to Director J'onzz if anyone who's been in contact with your brother at any point approaches you."

"We will make sure of that Madam President," Alex says, straightening her back to a painful point.

"I was talking to Miss Luthor, Agent Danvers."

Duly chastised, Alex looks to her feet ; as for Lena, she almost snarls. "I'd rather not be constantly monitored by a government agency," she says.

"This is a highly sensitive situation Miss Luthor, I would hope you cooperate with us."

"I will cooperate," Lena replies curtly, "but I will neither be monitored nor coddled."

"Excellent," the president says. "Then we have an agreement and I will be on my way. Supergirl ? A word please."

President Marsdin turns on her heels, her team seamlessly putting itself into motion around her. Kara jumps to a start, stumbles gracelessly and hurries after her.

"You will keep an eye on her, will you ? I have become quite fond of Miss Luthor and her work and I would be remiss if something were to happen to her."

"Frankly Madam President, the assumption that I would do anything else is rather offensive," Kara replies in a commanding tone.

The president pats her arm with a disconcerting familiarity then says, her eyes briefly flashing in a peculiar way. "I'm on your side Supergirl."

Before Kara can really look at her, the presidential security detail tightens and she's left standing behind. Slowly, she turns away from the president's retreating form to walk back to her friends, trying to infuse, for a reason she doesn't quite get, a semblance of confidence in her gait. The moment she's within reach, Lena stops her pacing to fold herself between her arms and at the first whiff of her familiar scent, Kara forgets a little about all the mess surrounding them. "Do you want to go home ?" she asks quietly.

Lena nods, forgoing words for the moment, and with no other confirmation needed, Kara gathers her tight against her to shield her from the elements, and simply takes off, leaving everyone else behind. There will be time later for complicated security plans, for now, she thinks they both just need some quiet.

***

The day passes by in a rather uninteresting manner. They take a nap upon coming home then walk Krypto and have a late breakfast before huddling in front of the TV to watch reruns of The L Word that Lena fondly criticises while Kara dozes on and off, startling awake what feels like every minute or so. In the late afternoon, they have a bath and an early dinner, then walk Krypto and go to bed where Kara does not fall asleep.

She simply can't. Her body refuses to relax and her hearing is tuned into every minute sound, her overworking brain classifying a fly on the wall three buildings away as a threat. Then, there's the buzzing. The one that she's learned to tune out again but that she sometimes can't help but hear, ever-present and overbearing. She hears it now, her own body driving her to the point of madness as she tosses and turns, trying to make it quiet.

Lena is sleeping lightly beside her, her hand periodically reaching out to rest soothingly on her arm before Kara twists again, this way or that. Eventually, she decides to just get up. She knows there's a chance her disappearance will cause Lena to wake up too, but for now she'll take the chance of allowing her to rest without a restless furnace next to her. She pads out of the room, steps over Krypto who immediately rouses to follow her, and, after prying open the heavy door of the apartment, she makes her way to the roof, her dog in tow.

She plops down on the ledge, on the spot that has become worn and smooth from her sitting. Krypto comes up next to her, resting his head next to her thigh and yawning as he settles in what can't possibly be a comfortable position. He cocks his head to the side, watching her with warm brown eyes, and sighs deeply when she smoothes her hand on his short soft fur after booping his nose.

"I know buddy," she whispers apropo of nothing and everything all at once, "I know."

He blinks at her in understanding, and she sighs too.

They stay like that, just the two of them, until midnight strikes on a clock in a nearby apartment and Lena pads out on the roof, messy hair and lithe frame wrapped in one of Kara's old plaid shirts. She comes sit next to her, stepping over the ledge to let her feet dangle in the air. She's wearing mismatched fluffy socks, one of them a little too big for her and slipping down precariously. She lowers her head down on Kara's shoulder, mumbles "I can't sleep without you," then sighs too.

"Sorry," Kara whispers, dropping a kiss on the crown of her head then wrapping an arm around her to keep her safe from the chill air of the night, "I'll come back to bed soon."

"Do you want to talk about it ?" Lena asks sleepily, "or just sit for a while ?"

"I just," Kara starts, waving her hand around with restrained anger, "I'm tired."

"I get it. The world is a trashcan on fire," Lena says wisely.

Kara snorts, holds onto her a little tighter.

"I'm sorry about the gala."

"Lena, you can't possibly hold yourself responsible for being attacked."

"Maybe if I'd picked up the phone when Lex called," Lena says wearily, letting the rest of her thoughts trail into nothing.

"No," Kara says firmly, "no. This is not your fault, this was never your fault. If anything," she continues, trying to keep her voice from slipping into an inaudible whisper, "it's mine."

"What ?!" Lena exclaims, straightening up so abruptly that only Kara's arm around her body prevents her from tipping over the edge.

"You know it's true," Kara sighs. "Lex is not a renowned Kryptonian lover. I put you in danger. I put everyone in danger."

"And yet," Lena replies, unwavering, "I'd choose you every single day."

"Lena..."

"That's not up for discussion. I choose you. Hell or high water. And when it comes to it, I know you'll be able to protect me, just like I know I can protect you."

"I suppose you're right," Kara says, deflating a little.

Lena hums. "It happens from times to times," she replies. "But I'm also still fuzzy from the painkillers so..." She stops, laughs a little. "It's just, as long as I have you, I feel like anything is possible. Together, there's nothing we can't face and we already proved it. I just want to have a little faith in what we can do." She turns to drop a kiss on Kara's shoulder, lingers there for a moment breathing in the flowery smell of their shared laundry detergent. "It doesn't mean I'm not scared, hell, I'm terrified, but together, I think we're unbreakable."

"Unbreakable," Kara echoes softly.

"Yes. Hell or high water. Now, come back to bed ?"

Kara leaves this simple question hanging for a moment, then replies an even simpler "okay," and, unfolding herself from her position on the ledge, gathers Lena in her arms and carries her back to bed. Still restless, she glances over her shoulder as they exit the roof, but there's nothing behind her but Krypto and the near silent sound of his paws on the floor. For tonight, maybe they are safe.

Notes for the Chapter:

In case Tumblr is more your thing than Twitter I'm also on it though not a lot because I often forget about it ^^ You can follow me there if it's your social media of choice : ClaraZorEl.

6. Disappear for a while (Lena)

Summary for the Chapter:

In which Kara and Lena escape to Midvale for a little while.

Notes for the Chapter:

I don't know where Midvale is supposed to be in the show. I've taken the habit of placing it somewhere around Monterey, California, so this is where it is in this story as well.

Title is from Disappear by Tonight Alive.

She hasn’t seen Lex in years. Except in pictures of course, in newspapers and tabloids, and in the faded photographs she kept and can't help but look at from time to time. But she hasn't seen him like this in a long time, alive, moving, breathing, strangely present even through the TV screen. He's still bald, but his beard has grown a few inches, maybe to hide the hollowness of his cheeks. She stares, transfixed, at the man who isn't quite her brother walking in between heavily armed guards up to a reinforced van. The video is filmed from inside the prison and the transfer happened hours ago, monitored by Supergirl in person, but she still expects him to break free and find her here. He doesn't, but he does look straight at the camera, and it feels a lot like a warning.

She can feel Kara squirming next to her, her tall frame folded onto the couch as she tries to stop herself from fidgeting. She's relinquished the remote to Lena, giving her full control to just turn off the TV and walk away ; but Lena needs to watch. She needs to watch and make sure Lex is taken and locked away somewhere he can't get to her, get to them. She is aware, in some distant part of her brain, that her behaviour right now borders on morbid fascination, but she can't help it. She also feel bad for putting Kara in this position, for having her there with her when she knows that she was a prime witness to Lex's descent into madness. To her credit though Kara, perfect Kara, doesn't complain but simply remains at her side, uncomfortable, but present and loving and reassuring ; Lena will find a way to make it up to her.

They're watching the report on mute ; neither of them need to know what's being said. They've already declined multiple interviews and Kara refused to report on the situation, reminding everyone for what to Lena feels like the thousand time that her focus is on science. A couple of people at the Tribune did try to argue that Lex Luthor relates to science in several ways but according to Nia, the sight of Kara's biceps bulging through her shirt shut them up rather quickly. Part of Lena wishes people would know better, the other knows how much the crowd loves drama.

It's one of the reasons she had to be shut away during his initial trial. She was cleared after one hearing and a deep dive into her personal life but not everyone let it go that easily. She remained in protective custody for a long time, sheltered not only from Lex's vengeful goons but from everyone out there seeking some macabre form of entertainment.

She still shudders when she thinks about the day Lex disappeared. She remembers stepping inside of her apartment after class, fumbling for the awkwardly positioned light switch and feeling glass creaking under her shoes. She remembers turning the lights on to find her home wrecked, looking down to find under her feet a picture of Andrea that she kept out of bizarre sentimentality, smudged with mud. She remembers looking up too, to find half a dozen men in armour standing in her living room, and being dragged away with a burlap sack on her head, and the months that followed, sheltered inside "for her own protection." She won't let that happen again.

"I won't let him or anyone hurt you," Kara says beside her and Lena startles, dragged out of her ghastly daydream.

She releases her grasp on the remote and turns the TV off. Krypto perks up at the sudden change in light but, deeming it unimportant, settles his head back on his paws with a quiet sigh. "I know," she says, "I trust you. But where President Marsdin is sending him, neither of us will need protection."

She chooses not to dwell on how fake and sour the words taste in her mouth.

***

It gets worse ; which on insight, Lena should have expected. The attack on the gala isn't has easy to hide as a bomb planted in her office or a discreet attempt at an abduction. Words get out of the big mastermind behind it, in part because of Marsdin power play, and the morning that follows Lex's transfer, their entire street is blocked by reporters and they have to take the sky route to their respective jobs.

It doesn't die down for an entire week ; and when it does, general interest extinguishing after a very bland statement on Lena's good health and L-Corp's lack of tie with Mister Luthor, she can't help but notice the two brand new DEO agents trailing her everywhere. It doesn't bother her as much as she thought it would. It's still taxing, and it's far from being an ideal situation, but it reassures Kara and she has to admit that maybe not dying in horrifying circumstances is a good thing. 

The agents don't come inside the apartment, they don't go through her things, they don't put their feet on her coffee table ; instead, there is an underlying current of trust that would be acceptable if Lena was the only one with increased security. But they're outside Kelly and Alex's house too, and she spots three undercover bodyguards outside of Ruby's school when she comes pick her up. She doesn't even want to think about what it must be like for Eliza, who already had to install state of the art alarms all around the house after several idiots tried to get inside Supergirl's childhood bedroom. 

It's the thing Kara feels worse about, the toll her superheroing is taking on her family, and now Lena has silently joined her in her guilt. They both know Eliza doesn't mind, that she’s just happy that Kara gets to be herself in every way, but there is something about the fact that her sort of mum can't go to bed without lowering metal screens in front of all the windows that makes Lena deeply uncomfortable.

On her better days, when she's had a successful board meeting and Kara swings by for lunch babbling about averting an eco disaster by lifting a sinking nuclear submarine off the water, bits of of seaweeds still stuck in her hair, Lena can see all this protection as a necessary evil. Today however, is not one of these days. Today, Kara finishes her weekly phone call to her mum with a forlorn look on her face and she still has remnants on her cheek of a lipstick that isn't Lena's, curtesy of the public' rampant horniness towards her hero, and she suddenly gets sick of it. Half an hour later, she slaps on the table two brand new baseball caps and two tickets for the SRS, the new high speed train dumbly dubbed Superspeed Railway System.

Kara looks up from her tablet, blinking owlishly at her with the air of someone who's been violently dragged out of deep thinking. Her mouth opens, forming the beginning of a question, but Lena cuts her off, heart thumping hard in her ears at her own impetuousness. She refuses to give herself the time to reconsider this.

"We're going away for the week-end."

Kara peers down at the train tickets, absentmindedly brushing a tuft of hair to the side. "If you want to go see Mum in Midvale," she says, "I could always fly us there."

"Let me reformulate then," Lena says quickly, her heart ready to take off through her chest, "we are disappearing for the week-end. Just the two of us. No bodyguard, no reporters. I have mud to disguise Krypto and shitty baseball caps."

Kara stares at her, inquisitive, and the extent of her retort are two simple syllables. "Alex ?"

"Already warned her. Everyone who needs to know knows."

A beat passes during which Kara seems intent on peeling back the layers of her soul with her bottomless blue eyes.

"Please," Lena pleads.

Kara turns off her tablet and rises from her chair a bit too quickly for human's eyes. "Okay," she says, much too softly for the way her jaw is clenched. "Just let me pack my bag."

***

Mrs and Mrs Kieran and their scruffy brown dog get on the train at National City Central. It's an hour long journey up to Midvale, longer than it would take by flight, but much quicker than the seven hours it would take by car. Baseball caps shoved on their heads up to their eyes, hunched shoulders and pressed gaits, they don't exactly look inconspicuous and though it was Lena's idea, she's on the brink of fainting up to the moment they drop heavily in their first class armchairs, giggling nervously. Lena feels better the moment she sinks into her seat. Kara folds the armrest and beckons her towards her warm embrace letting her shuffle and wiggle to her heart's content until she's comfortable.

"I think you had the right idea," she says, "a weekend away will do us both good."

She tries to lean in to kiss her on the cheek, but is stopped comically by her cap getting in the way. She glances around surreptitiously and once a family of four has finished walking by, removes it for a swift and sweet kiss before shoving it again on her head. The visor plunges her face in shadows, darkening her eyes and sharpening her jaw dangerously. Lena cuddles into her side, not resisting the urge to lay a hand on her firm stomach, and closes her eyes for the rest of the trip.

Eliza is there to pick them up at Midvale’s train station. She hugs them both tight on the platform, face cautiously obscured by a her own faded red cap, and leads them to a light blue truck. The car is perfectly normal and indistinct, except for the fact that it's bulletproof. They drive up the long winded cliff road, the one that has become familiar to Lena over the course of their last few visits, and finally pull up on the gravel alley of a neat yet bustling garden.

Lena hasn't visited Midvale many times, but every time she's here, there is something different about Eliza's garden ; a new flower bed, lanterns that are arranged differently along the path. Today there's a dark patch of fresh soil and as Kara idly unloads the car, her mother excitedly prattles on about the geranium she's thinking about having there. Lena herself doesn't know much about flowers, but there's something about the older woman babbling about her garden that nudges at her memory. She wonders if, like Eliza's, her birth mother's hands smelled like damp earth and sunshine. She must look more forlorn than intended, because when Kara walks past her, duffel bag carelessly thrown over her shoulder, she stops to grab her hand delicately, and lays a kiss on her cheek.

"Come on," she says, "Mum said she'd make hot chocolate."

There is indeed hot chocolate inside, rich and dark, not too sugary, exactly the way Lena likes it. Kara of course, dumps an enormous amount of whipped cream on top of hers and then proceeds to demolish the beverage with complimentary cookies. She makes a mess of her face, but wipes it all off before she dares kissing her while Eliza pointedly has her back turned to them. She knows how much Lena hates sticky things, and is always careful of keeping herself clean but never makes a big show of how accommodating she is. She kisses her sweet and slow, strong hands framing her face and tongue tasting of chocolate and the mints she gnawed on during their trip ; and Lena wonders, not for the first time and certainly not for the last, how she managed to land a girl like that.

They go up to Kara's bedroom for a nap after that, both pretending they don't see the conspicuous sleek black car parked right across the house and settling onto the narrow bed. The mattress is so small that Lena can't fathom Kara ever fully fitting onto it, even as a teenager. She settles on top of her, torso acting as her pillow, and arms turning into a soothing weighted blanket.

"This was a good idea," Kara says just before she drifts off. "You always have amazing ideas."

They wake up a little after lunch time and Eliza feeds them a dozen sandwiches, which is to say, one for Lena and eleven for Kara, the only present person who would still feel hungry after a mid-morning chocolate ; and then they are shooed outside for a digestive walk. Revelling in their newfound and temporary anonymity they take the path down to the beach where they let Krypto roam free until he plunges in seaweed and turn a lovely dark green colour.

Lena sighs, grumbles "this is gonna be a mess to clean."

Kara shrugs, the motion causing Lena's body to lift up too as their arms are intertwined. "I'll do it."

"There's no way he doesn't smell like death."

Kara shrugs again. "I'll plug my nose. Do you want to get ice cream ?"

"Are you ever not hungry ?"

Kara seems to really consider the question for a second, her face the picture perfect of seriousness. "No," she eventually answers, cracking up a smile. "So, ice cream ?"

"I'll eat some of yours."

Kara stops abruptly, and it's only thanks to quick reflexes and an extensive knowledge of Kara's usual reactions that Lena doesn't face-plant into the wet sand. "Lena," Kara says slowly, mildly horrified, "I love you, but that's not going to happen."

Lena gets some of her ice cream.

They spend the afternoon walking around and window shopping until the early evening when it starts drizzling and they find refuge from the humidity in a somewhat ratty dinner in which the waitress doesn't look at them twice even when they persist in keeping their hats on and Krypto's wet fur slowly drips an ocean on the black and white floor. Kara gets a burger the size of a small hubcap and Lena an omelette that isn't uneatable.

She's not particularly hungry, but there's something so fulfilling about just sitting there in this shit restaurant watching her love demolish her food, blond hair slipping from a ratty baseball cap, an unshakable grin on her face as she sucks barbecue sauce from her solid fingers. Silently, she wonders if there is anything better than that, legs tangled under a peeling laminate table, indistinct folk music and that loud happy laugh she could never get tired off. She gets her answer no less than half an hour later when Kara presses her against the brick wall mere feet from the door, light and conversations spilling onto the pavement.

Her mouth is hot and insistent on her, her hands heavy on her hips and this is everything Lena’s never had ; small town, anonymity, and a love both so pure and so eager that her feelings could swallow her whole. Desire burns low in her stomach and she wraps her arms against Kara's shoulders, using the leverage to lift herself on her toes, pressing her body against hers and hoping, maybe, that she will consume her if she tries hard enough.

They separate to the crass sound of a drunk dude wolf whistling and Kara shoulder-checks him as they walk away, hand casually slipped in Lena's back pocket.

Eliza is already in bed by the time they get back, a ray of light showing underneath her door but the rest of the house dark except for a single table lamp shining in the living room. Lena really hopes the older woman's hearing is starting to decrease, because she rapidly discovers the joy of sex on a single bed, and she's never been known for being exceptionally quiet.

***

Lena intends to sleep in. Unfortunately, her naked body makes contact with the cold hard floor at barely 7am when she attempts to roll around on the bed. Kara does not hide her hilarity as she helps her back on the mattress but she more than makes up for it with sweet kisses that carry them well into the morning.

When they finally get up, they find Eliza doing her crosswords in the kitchen, the dregs of her coffee abandoned next to a plate of crumbs. She's sitting in a lone ray of sunshine, a concentrated frown deepening the wrinkles on her forehead and she looks so much like her daughter that if Lena didn't already know about Kara, she'd truly believe they're related.

"Tend to, seven letters," the older woman says in lieu of a greeting, squeezing Kara's hand when she walks by.

Lena drags a chair to sit next to her, letting their shoulders brush, and looks down at the black and white grid. "Nurture ?"

Eliza hums, straightens her glasses then scribbles down the word. "It fits. Thank you sweetie. Did you sleep well ?"

Lena answers by the affirmative, gratefully taking a sip from the mug her girlfriend offers her. The coffee is a tad bitter and she stirs in a drop of milk watching as it turns a hazelnut colour. "I always do when I'm here," she replies.

"Good then. Any plans for today ? The weather looks promising."

"What time did you say our train was leaving ?" Kara asks.

Lena racks her brain, trying to remember if she mentioned it or if it skipped her mind the moment they stepped foot in the little coastal town. "I didn't," she says, "but I got us tickets for the 6:29 train tomorrow morning. It should leave us enough time to get to work. Is that okay ?" She asks her question quietly, staving off a sudden spike of anxiety.

"Very much so," Kara answers, setting before her a single crispy waffle topped with berries and just a dollop of whipped cream. "They've started setting up the fair on the pier. It's not too crowded this early in the season if you want to check it out."

Lena does the math quickly ; balancing the possibility of a multitude of sweaty people against the sole thought of Kara showing off at a silly game, cotton candy on the corner of her mouth. Kara wins, of course.

Midvale's annual fair is unlike anything Lena has ever seen. Though if she's being honest with herself, the closest she's ever been to a fair was when she snuck out of her boarding school for Saint Patrick's Day and threw up on top of a ferris wheel. Andrea laughed about it for weeks.

Baseball cap firmly in place, Kara leads her through the stalls, swinging their joined hands between their bodies. She's got a certain spring in her step, and a worry free smile stretches on her tan lovely face. She's already gobbled two waffles and washed them down with an extra large hot chocolate and when she kissed her earlier, surreptitiously in between two stacks of cardboard boxes, she tasted faintly of cinnamon. They left Krypto with Eliza and she at first was afraid that Kara, or herself really, wouldn't be able to cope, both now unused to being out without their dog, but they're doing fairly well. They haven't tried any game yet, mainly because Kara was busy with her second breakfast, and they stroll lazily, the scent of the sea not yet covered by the potent smell of fried food. They walk past a sea gull thoroughly decapitating a waffle cone and Lena wonders, briefly and wistfully, if in another universe this could be her life. She's barred from further self-inquiry by Kara stopping dead on her tracks in front of a shooting stand.

"Alex isn't here," she says, slamming a five dollar bill on the counter, "so there's no one to stop me from winning."

Ruffling in the pocket of her too tight jeans, Lena extracts her own bill and slams it on the counter next to Kara's, not harder because she physically can't, but with conviction. "My father put a gun in my hands within two weeks of my adoption. You're going down Danvers."

She grabs and arms the rifle before her, brings it to shoulder level and shoots clean through the flimsy cardboard with overt swagger. Kara turns to look at her, mouth slightly agape, pupils slightly dilated and fumbles to arm her own rifle, her nimble hands suddenly clumsy. She takes her shot, misses the bullseye by a good inch and turns again to look at her with a pout.

"That's unfair," she whines, "you distracted me."

"And how exactly did I distract you ?" Lena asks, biting back a laugh. "I'm just existing there."

Kara stammers, broadly gesturing at her silhouette with zero eloquence. She huffs, straightens her shoulders and takes aim again, this time putting the bullet straight through the centre. She doesn't miss any of her remaining shots, but Lena doesn't miss any at all which means in her book she wins even if the stall holder hands them both mildly terrifying teddy bears in Super outfits. Kara immediately decides that the bears are girlfriends, and though Lena is a little peeved by the general aspect of the plushies, she can't deny that it's cute.

They stop at nearly every stand and partake in almost every game ; Kara winning her a cheap keychain after fishing a plastic duck out of an inflatable pool and Lena purchasing a little bottle full of "real Midvale sand !" that reads Made in China on the bottom. Lunch consists of several hot dogs, most of them for Kara, and a locally made soda that rots her teeth right out of her gums and leaves a strange sour taste in her mouth. There's cotton candy after that and chocolate dipped waffles but Lena absolutely refuses to put anything else in her stomach. Kara might be a god-like bottomless pit but she isn't and though she tries not to monitor her weight too much, she still needs to fit in her suits if she wants to impress her board. In any case, she can taste this food right off of Kara's lips every time she leans in for a quick kiss, fingers dipping slightly into her waist.

They have a bit of a debate towards the end of their day out, when Lena's feet are starting to divorce her, whether it's right or not for Kara to take a turn at the high striker. But it's their one normal day for probably a very long time and in the end, Kara decides she'd like to try. She removes her shirt for show, leaving her in a skin tight black tank top and before she takes hold of the flimsy hammer, she bends Lena back in a long hard kiss, "for luck." Her muscles quiver with the strength she's holding back, and, after a second of pretend struggle, she strikes hard enough that Lena can see a tiny fracture on the bell. They walk out of the stand with an outrageously big purple fluffy bunny that moans "I love you," in a creepy voice when Lena presses its paw. She already loves it dearly, though she wouldn't admit it over her dead body.

She hauls the plushy beside her with some difficulty, keeping it clutched tightly against her side. At a souvenir stall, Kara buys it its own matching anonymity baseball cap and Lena laughs so much her cheeks hurt. She knows the day is drawing to a close, and with it, their short respite from their real lives, and she doesn't want to go home. This is why, she thinks, she doesn't mention her slight fear of heights when Kara nudges her towards the dingy ferris wheel.

They huddle inside of a small damp cabin, Lena still dragging her plush bunny and Kara stuffing her backpack between her legs, and it hasn't even started moving yet that she already knows she's going to be sick. She can feel bile rising in her throat and the world blurs slightly as her blood pumps loudly in her ears. Kara grabs her hand, lays a gentle kiss on her knuckles, and the death trap starts its ascension.

"Are you alright ?" Kara asks softly when they're close to the top and the carriage sways a little in the wind.

"Perfectly fine," Lena mumbles, lying blatantly through her clenched teeth.

"Are you sure ?" Kara probs, "you look a little green in the face."

Lena breathes in sharply, and makes the informed decision of keeping her mouth shut lest she pukes all over her girlfriend.

"Lena, are you afraid of heights ?"

Lena shakes her head. Or nod. She isn't sure.

"I'm so sorry," Kara says quickly, her words slurring a little in her hast. "You've always seemed fine on the roof and I never thought to ask."

She grabs her hand again, then the other, squeezing them tight. It works a little, Lena feeling less fleeting and fragile when she's anchored this way to this virtually indestructible being.

"I'm fine when it's sturdy," she says, breathing in deep through her nose and then exhaling slowly through her mouth. "Solid. This feels like it's going to collapse at any time."

"Oh no," Kara says, "the wheel’s been there for decades, we never had an accident. It's very safe. Very solid."

She's clearly aiming for reassurance, but the fact that the ride is probably older than Lena is not in fact comforting at all. "Not helping," she mumbles, squeezing her eyes shut.

The cabin lurches to a stop. They must be on top now but Lena refuses to check.

"Is now a bad time to tell you I paid them to let us admire the view ?"

Lena groans, and Kara lets out a strangled uncomfortable laugh.

"I'm so sorry," Kara says again. "I should have asked."

"It's okay darling." Lena risks an open eye, keeping her gaze firmly on Kara. "You were trying to be romantic and it's lovely. It's not your fault."

The cabin wobbles again and Lena spares a cursory glance to the ground before all but launching herself at Kara to hide her face in the crook of her neck. This, of course, has the foreseeable effect of causing the whole structure to sway dangerously.

Lena squeals. "I don't want to die."

Kara laughs, and tilts her head up, peering down at her with briny blue eyes. "You're not going to die," she says very softly. "You survived a trip aboard an unapproved spaceship, you'll survive a little ferris wheel."

She kisses her then, slowly, wielding Lena's lips with her own until she can slip her pliant tongue inside. Lena is almost sure she tastes like bile ; still, she falls into the moment, and when Kara draws back, they’re on solid ground again. "See," she says, "not so bad."

Lena does not hold back her murderous glare.

They end their day with dinner in the sort of restaurant that only seems to exist in alternative dimensions ; a hole in the wall with bland neon lights that serves a mix and match of defrosted food. Kara gets soy sauce on her nose ; Lena laughs until she cries.

They don't sleep much that night, not by lack of trying, but because there is a nervous tightness in Lena's chest at the idea of going back to the real world. She feels nauseous, despite the peppermint tea Eliza made her upon coming home, and Kara spends long hours rubbing small circles on her back. There's a joke on the tip of her tongue about pregnancy, but she worries it would fall flat and so does not make it. When she wakes up, early enough to catch their train, she feels like she hasn't slept at all.

Despite the ungodly hour, Eliza drives them back to the station. She waits for the train with them, buying them too hot coffee and flaky pastries before sending them off on the platform with motherly hugs and the promise to visit again soon. Krypto whines quietly when she walks away and Kara bends down to scratch him between the ears then wipes her hands on her jeans to get rid of the mud they reapplied on him. She steps on the train, turns around to help Lena up though it's charmingly unnecessary and then freezes. "I love you," she says with a bizarre intensity that Lena doesn't know what to make of. "I love you," she repeats, quieter ; and the moment passes.

***

/She shivers in the cold, skin rising in little bumps and even purple in places. She shuffles her feet in the freezing sand, letting the little grain pass between her toes. She wants to go home. She wants to go home but her mother said to wait for her, that she would be back soon. She hasn't surfaced from underneath the water, and the big hand on Lena's plastic watch has already made its way around half of it. She's starting to feel cold, but her mother said to wait for her./

Lena startles awake, remnants of a painful dream slipping away fast. Kara is standing over her, hunched to recover their bags from the overhead luggage rack.

"You're awake," she says with a wide loving smile. "We're just coming into the station."

Lena hums noncommittally, stretches and smirks when she catches Kara glancing at the sliver of skin uncovered by her shirt.

"How do you feel about a second breakfast ?" Kara asks, extending her hand to help her up.

Lena heaves herself to a standing position, stumbling a little under the pull of the train's brakes. Without letting go, she threads their fingers together, kisses her shoulder once, twice. "Sure," she says, "I can have some tea while you attempt to fill your bottomless stomach."

Notes for the Chapter:

I don't know if you remember from Dreamboat but Kara used to have pretty "interesting" dreams that turned out to not be dreams at all. This time, it's Lena's turn, meaning all of her dreams are actually memories. Enjoy the ride 🙃

7. Sit with you in the trenches (Kara)

Summary for the Chapter:

In which a heat wave smothers National City, Lena's middle name is Foreshadowing, and she is forced in a situation she never thought she'd find herself in.

Notes for the Chapter:

Title is from Peace by Taylor Swift 🙃

Content warning : Starting from this chapter onward there'll be some discussion of terminal illnesses.

Kara stares at the bottom of her Saturnian whiskey, condensation pooling around her hand. The feedback from her prosthetic informs her that the glass is cold, but the liquid burns warmly down her throat when she swallows it. It's expensive, and not just because it's imported from off-world ; Aldebaran rum can be quite cheap, but Lena only ever buys her top shelf drinks. Jack stops talking, finally aware that she stopped listening to him the moment Lena had to step out to take a call from work ; something about an attempted breach on a secure server. Kara flags down the bartender, orders another drink for herself and a double for Lena whose heartbeat is wading its way back through the crowd ; she's bound to be in a fool mood now. They've been home for barely a week, and things are already taking a turn for the worse, almost like Lex's brief but explosive reappearance has cast a shadow over them.

Lena hops onto her stool and immediately leans into her, groaning. Out of automatism, Kara's hand comes rub circles on her shoulders, attempting to reduce the tension that has built there.

"It's patched for now. But I'll have to come in early tomorrow morning."

"So like every day then," Jack remarks with a hint of teasing.

"Earlier," Lena replies dryly. She takes a sip of her drink, then another, and sets the glass back on the counter with a light controlled clink.

Kara frowns, preemptively mourning the loss of a quiet morning together. She supposes she'll just go to work early herself, get a quick start on her own day ; but there's nothing she likes as much as being home with Lena.

Though she isn't looking at her, Lena picks up on the shift in mood, and she straightens up to kiss her softly on the jaw once, then another time, just below her ear. "Sorry darling," she murmurs, "I'll make it up to you."

Kara has no doubt that she will.

And in fact she does, as soon as Jack has abandoned their bi-monthly whiskey outing to pursue a muscle mass of a man and they're both drunk enough to think having sex in a public bathroom is a good idea. Lena goes down on her in a wide black marble stall and Kara bites straight through her synthetic skin trying to keep quiet when a group of chatty women walk in to wash their hands. She won't mind if this particular wound takes a bit of time to heal.

Lena is gone early the next morning, earlier even than Kara though she would be. She hears her moving around the apartment then slipping back into their bedroom for a short bout of her ritual counting, but doesn't move after Lena gently pushes her back under the covers. When she gets up, she finds Krypto in the kitchen, left behind and wistfully staring at an unopened box of donuts with a sticky note on top. I'll be home late tonight. Don't wait up for me. I love you. L. She keeps the note in her pocket for the entire day.

It takes Lena and her team almost two weeks to trace back the cyberattack, going from decoy to decoy and hitting walls after walls. The worst has been avoided, but she refuses to let it go, digging deeper and deeper every time she has a free second. They cancel date night twice, and it takes a lot of convincing to get her to come to game night. Kara takes it in stride, bending when she needs to bend and coddling when she needs to coddle and never once snapping, not even when Lena gets back up at 2am to run a line of code that she swears is familiar. When summer rolls around with its heat and anxiety and the DEO is enlisted to storm a warehouse in the middle of the desert, she's proven right when all they find is a picture of Lex Luthor on a polished metal table. A third agent is added to Lena's security detail, then a fourth, when an analysis ran on the picture reveals it's covered in her own DNA.

***

Lena produces a little sound, midway between a sigh and a groan. Actually, she sounds a little bit like Krypto when he yawns, but Kara doesn't feel like making a joke right now. It's close to 1am now, and the temperature has yet to drop to an acceptable level. Lena is sweating through every pore of her body and Kara doesn't need to be able to read her mind to know she's trying to solve all the world's problems in her state of semi-consciousness. She begins to reach out, then remembers how warm her hands usually are and retreats fast, not wanting to overwhelm the fragile human body lying next to her.

"Do you want me to run you another bath ?" she asks, her voice barely over a whisper yet so loud in the heavy quietness of the night. "Freeze breath ?"

Lena gasps, springing up like a jack-in-the-box ; if Kara could have a heart attack on this planet, she surely would have had one right now.

"Fuck. Shit. Fuck."

"Sorry," Kara mumbles, "didn't mean to wake you up."

"M'not sure I was sleeping." She yawns, her jaw popping back into place with a snapping sound. "Can't take a bath now. We have to be up early tomorrow."

"Tomorrow's Sunday. We don't have to be up at all."

"Oh," Lena says, almost silently, "in that case, a bath sounds nice."

"Don't move," Kara says, extirpating herself out of the bed, "I'll be back in a minute."

Lena only hums in reply, and in a dash, Kara is in a bathroom, holding her hand impatiently under a tepid flow of water. She has half a mind of calling her mum again, but they got off the phone not two hours before and with a bit of luck, the older woman managed to fall asleep. It's supposed to be a bit cooler in Midvale ; maybe they should take another trip there. She blinks, realises she hasn't plugged the bathtub and before doing so, blows a thin sheet of ice on its sides.

Lena pads in the bathroom, eyes half closed to fight the brightness reflecting off the white enamel. She yawns again, stretching her arms over her head, her sleep shirt riding up in the process to reveal a pair of Kara's old boxers. Her skin is flushed from the heat, her hair a little damp from her sweat. She looks absolutely perfect.

She doesn't wait for the bath to be fully drawn to step into it, uncharacteristically leaving her clothes in a messy pile on the floor. She shudders at the coldness of the water but still sinks into it, attempting to submerge herself in the few inches.

"Bloody hell."

Kara picks up the clothes without a word, folding them neatly and laying them on the counter before sitting on the edge of the tub. "There's a storm in the desert blocking the airflow on the coast," she says. "It should be on us by tomorrow."

"I should be doing more," Lena whispers, relaxing in the water.

"You're doing everything you can." Kara dips her hand in the water, checking the temperature, and turns the tap off. "It's not your fault humans are foolish and refuse to stop using fossil fuel."

She frowns as she says this, trying her hardest not to think about Krypton. Technically speaking, the summer temperatures have been stable for two years now thanks to tremendous effort helmed by L-Corp, so there is an improvement, but they’re also not lowering, and sometimes, she fears it's too late for Earth.

She cards her wet hand through Lena's hair, undoing a knot at the base of her skull. Without meaning too, she mirrors the gesture in her own ; it's starting to be a bit long, she'll need to ask Alex to do something about it soon.

Lena blinks, then yawns once more but with less power ; she's starting to fall asleep. "If tomorrow is Sunday," she starts, stuttering a little, "we have brunch, right ?"

Kara nods. "Do you want me to cancel ?"

"No," Lena whispers, "I've barely had time to see anyone lately, if I don't catch up Alex is going to storm my office again."

Kara chuckles, and Lena tries to level her with a glare. "That she will."

"I still feel like I'm missing something."

Kara represses a sigh, turning her back to grab a clean fluffy towel. "You went over this dozens of times. You said nothing was missing."

"Never mind," Lena says, shaking her head in discomfit as she steps out of the bathtub and into the towel. "I'm just stressed. Or that's what my therapist says."

"I think," Kara says gently, "that your therapist might be right about this. I don't mean that in a bad way. Just maybe that what happened recently might be wrapping your perspective a little."

Lena sighs deeply. "You're right."

"Lex can't get to you, to us, anymore from where he is now."

Somehow, this feels like a lie.

"You're right," Lena repeats, shaking her head slowly. She looks up with a tentative smile, "take me to bed ?"

***

The next morning finds them both at brunch, sitting across the Danvers-Olsen couple and their now semi-permanent addendum Sam ; Kara isn't sure what’s going on with that and Alex has yet to talk to her about it. Not from a lack of trying on her part, but the last time she tried to prob, Alex almost took out her ear with the clippers and she would really like to not lose another appendage. Ruby has been entrusted to stay home alone with her video games but both Sam and Alex have their phone face up on the table, just in case.

It's barely 10am but the temperature is already smothering, heat rising from the pavement in puffs of steam that might even be visible to the human eye. The air around Kara smells of hot concrete and old sweat and she observes as the people around her go about their day in as little clothing as is socially acceptable. Lena is sitting in the shade, looking positively murderous as she glares at her cup of tea like it's insulted her ancestors. A bead of sweat is slowly making its way down her temple and Kara knows that if one more indiscreet Sunday photographer takes a picture of her, she'll have to help her hide a body. Fortunately, Nia and Brainy come running before anyone can snap.

"Sorry," Nia says, huffing and puffing, "sorry. Overslept." She goes to sit but Brainy intercepts her, drawing her chair for her with a flourish. "That weather's a bitch," she says, plopping down on the offered seat with zero grace. "I'm melting."

"Technically speaking," Brainy interjects, sitting down with mechanical precision, "the human body cannot melt. However, if your core temperature reaches 104 F°, your internal organs can shut down and you will die."

Alex discreetly spits back her coffee in her cup.

"Thanks Brainy," Nia says, wiping her brow, "that's very reassuring."

"You are most welcome my love."

"It is hot though," Sam says, taking a long sip of her iced coffee. "Even I can feel it."

"Temperature is down 0,001 degree from last year at the same time," Brainy says, crossing his hands neatly before him.

At his words, Lena extracts a pen from the plunging cleavage of her flowing floral dress. She starts scribbling on a napkin at breakneck speed and Kara knows that she's lost her for the remainder of their brunch. With a light hand, she brushes away a couple of strands sticking to her neck then rests it on her favourite spot, her supple thigh. She hears the shutter of a camera and angles her body slightly to cover Lena from the street ; they're both tired of being on the news simply for breathing.

Brunch moves on around Lena and though Kara takes great care of putting food on her plate, she pays it little mind, only taking a bite here and there. Most of the time she misses her mouth entirely, soft yellow omelet dripping all over the table cloth. Kara picks it up every time to put it back on her own plate ; she knows Lena wouldn't like eating something that's been dropped like that.

Alex is looking at her quizzically but the glint in her eyes seems to be turned inward, her question directed at herself. She knows Kara would go to hell and back for Lena but who would she go to hell for ? Kelly ? Or Sam ? Kara will support her no matter what, but she'd still like to know sooner rather than later if her sister is going to crash and burn. Right now, even if she directs her gaze towards her wife, her body is angled towards Sam, and that spells nothing but trouble.

Kelly is in the process of recounting a joke Ruby told her when she picked her up from school this week, they’ve been taking turn doing that, to the point that the teenager now often casually says she has three mums, when Lena slaps her pen hard on the table, ink spurting from the tip and splattering in a wide black arc on the cream linen table cloth. "I can get it down by 32,8 by next year. 33 if I relocate a third of L-Corp's available resources to our climate change division."

"That would jeopardise our space exploration department," Sam points out but Lena ignores her pointedly turning instead to Brainy.

"How would you do that ?" he asks, delicately laying his coffee cup back in its saucer.

"I was thinking about my brother," Lena admits quietly, casting a hesitant glance around the table before going on when all she receives are encouraging nods. "When he started going mad," she says, choosing her words carefully, "he created a dispersion device that was to be used to flood the atmosphere with Kryptonite."

Kara tenses involuntarily at her words, and Lena briefly squeezes the hand that rests on her thigh before comfortingly threading their fingers together.

"Up until now, R&D has been working on it in an attempt to create a medicine aerosol that could be used to rapidly immunise entire populations in remote part of the world, the trick being that we would need to keep the medicine stable enough until it reaches the human system. Now, if I could reverse engineer that, it could be used to suck out noxious gases from the atmosphere."

"That would still be a lot of carbon to store somewhere else," Sam says, looking at some numbers on her phone. She turns to show the screen to Alex who nods a little too wisely to truly have understood anything that's going on. Kara almost laughs but manages to hold it back by turning to Lena instead.

"Oh no," Lena continues, turning her napkin over to reveal another string of numbers and formulas before saying something that coming from anyone else would simply be dismissed as a sleep deprived thought ; "I could make diamonds out of this."

Nia's eyebrows shoot into the stratosphere. "Dibs on the first one."

Brainy looks mildly disgruntled by the fact that he hasn't thought about this himself but his short bout of discontentment is promptly wiped out by Nia leaning in to whisper in his ear. "I'm sure Lena will give you a discount if you want to buy one for me."

Kara presses against her thigh then leans in to lay a soft kiss on her cheek. "You're a genius. I'm so proud of you."

Lena turns her head before Kara can retreat to her own space, their lips connecting for a short blissful moment. She has half a mind to deepen the kiss, present company and paparazzi be damned, when Lena's phone starts ringing with an ear splitting shrill. They jump apart from each other, Kara's chair creaking dangerously under her weight.

Quickly, Lena rejects the call, it's from an unknown number ; but her heartbeat still skyrockets painfully and she leans heavily against Kara's shoulder, attempting to ground them both via the other. From the other side of the table, Alex shoots them a questioning gaze but Kara shakes her head dismissively ; loud ringtones she can handle, it's vibrations that gets to her the most.

Lena takes a sip of her tepid tea and the brunch resumes its course, Nia launching into an anecdote about one of her latest fashion interview. Less than a minute later however, Lena's phone starts ringing again. Her hand creeps closer to it, frustration etched deeply into every part of her face and Kara can already picture her annihilating the poor unknown caller for getting their hands on her very restricted number. She gets a strange hunch though, just before Lena's hand touches the phone, and snatches it away from her.

"Kara Danvers speaking," she says harshly into the phone.

She's met with a short second of silence during which she can acutely feel all six of her companions staring at her then the line crackles, and she nearly breaks the phone in two.

"Miss Danvers, hi, I'm Doctor Hale, may I speak with Miss Luthor please, she's her mother's emergency contact."

***

It's freezing inside of the hospital, but Kara isn't entirely convinced this is why Lena is shivering so much. She's wrapped in the meagre flannel shirt Kara threw over her tank top when she got dressed this morning, the checkered fabric contrasting clownishly with her elegant summer dress. She keeps her hands tucked under her armpits as she stalks rapidly up the corridor following the tall doctor and her mass of golden hair.

Kara wishes she could hold her, shield her from whatever is on the other side of the door they just stopped in front of, but she knows she won't be able to. Not because the medical team will keep her out, Lillian apparently allowed Lena to come in with anyone she pleases, but because Lena herself won't let her. The moment they heard from the hospital, walls shot high around her and she retreated behind them, formulating only a curt sentence to ask Kara to come with her. There is a history of cancer in the Luthors, and though saying Lena isn't close to her adoptive mother is the understatement of the millennium, she isn't unaffected.

The doctor hesitates in front of the door and so does Kara. Ultimately, she decides to try to reach out anyway, tentatively putting her hand on Lena's shoulder. When Lena doesn't shrug her off but instead lean back against her, allowing herself to be embraced, a knot unwinds itself in Kara's chest.

"Your mother's condition is very serious," the doctor starts.

"Lillian isn't my mother," Lena cuts abruptly.

"Mrs Luthor's condition is very serious," the doctor tries again, a nervous tic showing at the corner of her mouth. "She's been following an intensive chemotherapy treatment to reduce the size of the tumour in the hopes of removing the rest surgically but her cancer has been progressing quicker than we anticipated. She'll need radiotherapy starting next week."

The doctor pauses here, undoubtedly expecting Lena to say something though what that something should be is a little unclear in Kara's mind.

"She's signed the papers deferring all choice to you in the event of her incapacitation," Doctor Hale continues, "and Miss Luthor, you should know the odds are not good."

Lena tenses, straightens up away from Kara's arms. "Do whatever must be done," she says, her voice devoid of emotion.

"She's stable for now, you can come in and see her."

For a moment, a few seconds lost in time, Kara thinks Lena is about to turn away and walk out of the hospital without looking back, but she reaches out for the handle with an unnaturally steady hand, and walks into the room. Kara follows a couple steps behind.

The room reeks of medication and sanitising products and Kara briefly wonders how anyone can handle being here before she remembers not everyone smells things as intensely as she does. Lillian is awake when they walk in. She's propped up against the pillows, eyes closed and skin ghastly in the greenish glow reflecting off the walls of the room. She turns her head minutely towards them when they enter the room, but it's as far as her acknowledgment of their presence goes for long minutes.

Lena hovers awkwardly for a moment before settling on the chair closest to the bed, her shoulders set back in an effort to project confidence. Kara settles in the other, an uncomfortable armchair of chromed metal and fake leather that seems to have been forgotten in a corner of the room.

"You came," Lillian says after a long moment, her words settling uncomfortably between a statement and a question.

"Of course I did," Lena replies quietly, her voice softer than Kara thought it would be.

Unwillingly, she's blasted back to the time, so long ago that it might as well belong to another life, when Lena confessed to not hating her mother, and for all the hatred she sometimes tries to project, it seems that she indeed doesn't.

"I assume Doctor Hale told you everything ?"

Lena nods. "Stage 3 pancreatic cancer," she says, her voice slipping from warmth to a certain clinical coldness. "It was discovered four months ago during your yearly routine check up. Treatment and recovery are-"

"I will be dead in eight months at most," Lillian cuts, poorly masking a slight tremor in her voice. "I've only accepted treatment to buy myself some time to tie up loose ends."

"Mother no !" Lena shouts, her facade briefly breaking before she schools herself at an alarming speed. Kara half rises from her chair, freezing in this awkward position for a moment before she lowers herself down again. "We've made leaps and bounds in cancer treatment," Lena continues, "especially pancreatic cancer. I'm sure something can be done."

Lillian smiles, the expression a strange sight on her artificially smoothed face. She finally opens her eyes. "Lena," she whispers, "I'm tired. So, so tired. Can't you understand that ?"

Lena opens her mouth to interrupt her but Lillian raises a shaking hand to silence her. "My life has been nothing but abject failure upon abject failure, and my only chance at redemption, the only thing I could have done right, I ruined too. I've failed you Lena, and that is the only thing I want to fix before I go. You don't have to let me of course, but I couldn't depart without you knowing that though- though I haven't been the best of mothers to you, I have loved you to the best of my abilities, and I'm sorry it wasn't enough."

She coughs and winces, her pale hand coming to rest on her abdomen. Lena again attempts to say something but Lillian again cuts her off. "You don't have to make a decision right now, you've given me so much already, but if you manage to see through all the pain I've caused you, well I'm still around for a few months."

"I," Lena stammers, "I- I need to go."

She springs up in a flurry of fabric, stumbling on the side of the chair before starting for the door with hurried anguished steps. She stops on the threshold, catching herself on the side of the door and whirling around to stare at the weary frame of her mother on the hospital bed. "This is not a no," she says timidly.

"You just need more time," Lillian says with the barest hint of hope.

"I just need more time," Lena echoes quietly before exiting the room, leaving behind nothing but the smell of an expensive perfume Lillian probably can't smell.

Kara stands up with more care. Slowly, she starts walking to the bed, but Lena's laboured breathing outside of the room has her changing course fast.

"Supergirl ?" Lillian calls out.

"Kara."

"Kara then," Lillian says. "Thank you, for being there for her. She’s- She’s- Don't let her go."

"I won't," Kara replies. In this moment, she knows they understand each other more than they ever will.

***

For once, Kara isn't the first one on the roof that night. She goes through her night time routine, quickly cleaning herself up and slipping into a pair of loose shorts and a soft cotton t-shirt that might have been Alex's once upon a time. She brushes her teeth twice, there was too much garlic on her pizza, and when she's done, Lena still hasn't come down. And she should have, the storm is almost upon them, thunder rolling in the distance, and being outside right now isn't the smartest thing to do.

Lena however, does not seem to be in the mood to do smart things right now. She's slept through part of the afternoon, effectively ruining her sleeping schedule, and has spent what little time she was awake tucked against Kara, near silent except for a couple of vague mumbles of acknowledgment. She's hurting, but she's also fallen too deep inside of her own mind and for the first time, Kara doesn't know where Lena's processing ends and where her self-loathing begins. What is she supposed to tell her anyway ? Everything is going to be okay ? That's a lie, and they would both know it. What do you tell someone whose estranged mother is about to die ? What fake niceties can you spout to someone who's about to lose the last person who saw them grow up ?

Kara sighs ; on the roof, so does Lena. Grabbing a light blanket from the couch, she makes her way out, the floorboard creaking under her weight. She finds Lena where she already was when she checked in on her after dinner, sitting cross-legged on the ledge, body haloed by the setting sun. Now isn't the time to ponder about how beautiful she is, but Kara takes a moment to do so anyway, hovering on the landing and just looking for a second.

Krypto raises his head at her arrival but Lena herself doesn't move one inch until Kara settles down next to her. Then, she leans tentatively against her shoulder, hair tumbling over her face. She makes no move to get it out of the way, so Kara does it for her, brushing her fingers on her cold skin.

"We need to go inside," she says softly. "Can't be outside when it starts raining."

"In a minute," Lena replies, her words audible only to Kara's superhearing. "I just need some air."

"Do you want me to go ?"

"I never want you to go," Lena whispers.

Kara kisses the side of her head and doesn't move again for a long time, lips pressed against her messy hair. "I'm right here," she murmurs eventually.

"I don't know what I'm supposed to do," Lena admits, clearing her throat loudly. "We were never close. And she was admittedly an horrendous mother. But if- if she's willing to try, shouldn't I allow her that ?"

"You don't owe her anything, and certainly not absolution."

"But...?" Lena probs hesitantly.

Kara breathes out, doesn't know if she should answer.

"What would you do ?"

"I-" She stops, closes her eyes for a minute. She thinks about Sam, about her blood oozing on Alex's hands, and shudders. "If it were me," she says, "and I know it's complicated but, if it were me, and I were given a second chance with someone who's hurt me like she's hurt you, I know I would regret not taking it. But I've lost everything once already, and that's why."

"I don't want her to die alone. I don't want her to die at all. But..."

"You don't have to decide right now, you have time."

"I don't," Lena bites back, "she's on borrowed time already. I have to make a choice. I have to make a choice right now."

"Do you think it could help you ?" Kara asks softly, "being there with her ?"

"I don't know," Lena breathes, "I think it could. Maybe. Maybe if I understand her, then I'll understand myself too. The parts that I've never wanted to really understand. She raised me after all. Poorly sure but she raised me."

Thunder cracks close to them, the flash of light greenish and blinding, and they both startle. The first drop of the promised rain falls on Kara's hand.

"You're right," Lena continues, "I should think about it. Maybe sleep on it. Do you think we could go to bed now ?"

But Kara isn't listening anymore. She feels something warm dripping down her face and when she brings her hand to her nose, it comes away covered in blood. She feels sick all of sudden, nauseated and unbalanced.

"Kara ?"

A green veil falls over her vision, the world around her vibrates. When she parts her lips to answer, she tastes blood on her tongue.

"Kara love, are you okay ?"

The question sounds very strange to Kara's ears, distorted, distanced. She doesn't think she's okay, turns to Lena to tell her just that in a calm voice. But as she goes to move, she tilts sideways, and the ground below rushes towards her at an incredible speed.

Notes for the Chapter:

Apparently there really is a company that plans on making diamonds with CO2 so I didn't completely pull that one out of my ass.

8. Without you by my side (Lena)

Summary for the Chapter:

In which some people get a severe case of Kryptonite poisoning, Alex has a small mental breakdown and Lena is an annoyed genius.

Notes for the Chapter:

Title is from Die for you by Starset. There's an acoustic version of it somewhere on Youtube if that's your thing.

FYI : editing is probably terrible in this chapter because I have adulthood related anxiety and couldn't concentrate on shit for the major part of the day.

For a long endless moment, an eternity that can't last more than a handful of seconds, what happens doesn't register properly in Lena's brain. She watches, befuddled as Kara pitches on the side of the building and doesn't take flight ; stares, helpless, as she lands in a crater and doesn't move. By the time she understands that she's not going to get back up, it's too late to act.

Krypto whines, her phone starts ringing, but she doesn't pick it up. The sky has opened in two, unleashing a storm of Kryptonite rain and tingeing everything in a sickly green colour. The air is acrid, it burns in Lena's lungs as she takes off down the stairs, going two steps at a time and bruising herself on walls and corners when she isn't fast enough to take a turn. She bursts through the back door and into the narrow alley, hands throbbing in pain from the momentum of throwing herself on the emergency handle and finds Kara writhing on the ground as she struggles to get back to her feet.

"Alex," she groans. A long spasm runs through her body, blood gurgles out of her mouth. "Need Alex."

Lena crouches beside her then stands up again abruptly, frantically patting her pockets for her phone. Before she can find it however a slick black van skids to a stop a couple of feet from them tail sending an overflowing dumpster flying away in a geyser of trash. It's not Alex who comes out of it but J'onn. He runs up to them and falls to his knees, immediately putting a hand on Kara's chest to pin her to the ground.

She struggles against it but can't lift up more than a couple of inches. "Alex," she mumbles. "Alex."

A shadow falls over J'onn's face and Lena's heart tightens in her chest. If Kara is already struggling to breathe then-

"She's with Ruby," he says, and with no more words, he collects her in his arms and runs back to the van.

Lena stumbles to her feet and hurries after him, climbing into the back of the car with a distinct lack of grace. The driver peels off the pavement before the door is even fully closed.

The inside of the van has been fully equipped with state of the art medical machinery and J'onn is already fitting a breathing mask over her face. Kara's eyes are glassy, green veins stretching over the white of her cornea. She fumbles for Lena's hand, fingers shaky and palm clammy until Lena herself grabs it for her, squeezing tight, too tight probably but her pulse is so weak that Lena has to cling to her to feel it.

"This won't hold on for long. We need to get her into containment."

Kara's free hand tentatively claws at the mask obscuring her nose and mouth but J'onn grabs it roughly and straps it down to the gurney.

"Don't," he grunts, "you'll only hurt yourself."

"You're going to be fine," Lena lies, trying to get a hold of her fluttering eyes, "I promise. You're going to be fine."

Kara whines. Blood speckles cover the inside of the oxygen mask.

"I'm going to have to intubate her," J'onn says, turning to Lena and retrieving a long sterilised and insulated package in the same flow. "And I should tell you that we have yet to retrieve Sam Arias."

"You haven’t what ?"

"She went flying. We lost track of her over the desert. The extraction team has yet to find her."

He delivers this information clinically, tearing open the breathing tube and removing Kara's oxygen mask at the same time.  The van goes over a bump, and at the change of sound outside the hull, Lena can tell they've just entered the DEO's underground parking. Kara only needs to hold on for a few more minutes.

"You're going to be okay," she repeats, squeezing her hand and hating herself more and more for the lie ; nothing is going to be okay. "Just stay with me. Please."

Kara's eyes close, slowly, like she's falling asleep and Lena absolutely refuses it. She refuses to lose her here, won't let her die in the back of a black op van, won't let this be the end of them.

"Don't you dare dying on me Kara. You can't leave me now, not again. Not again !"

The van stops, tires screeching on the waxed concrete and immediately its doors fly open, hands reaching inside for the gurney just as J'onn starts pushing the tube down Kara's throat.

It happens fast ; blink and you miss it. Kara's hand slips from Lena's grasp and when only a moment ago she was on the brink of death, she's now sitting gasping for air, the breathing tube crushed in her hand. She casts a wild glance around and backs up until she falls off the bed and onto the van's floor, back pressed against the driver seat. Her skin is no longer violently green but has turned a delicate pale mint.

"What-" she gasps, "what-"
