Immediately, Lena is at her side again, rubbing circles on her back and leaning all of her weight on her lap trying her best to ground her, to anchor her to something real and warm.

"You're okay," she murmurs. "You're okay love, breathe with me."

"Your techno-organic compounds must have kicked in," J'onn says coolly. "Come, we have lives to save."

"Give her a fucking minute," Lena snaps, forgetting for a fraction of second that Ruby and Sam are dying, that they don't even know where Sam is, to focus each and everyone of her atoms on Kara, on her breathing, slightly laboured but existent, and on the beat of her heart, wild and loud but so full of life.

"Where do you need me ?" Kara asks immediately, gently pushing Lena away from her so she can struggle to her feet. Her legs tremble under her weight.

J'onn cocks his head to the side, bringing two fingers to the comm device in his ear. "Great news," he says with a firm nod. "Good job everyone, bring her in to sub-level 19. We're going into lockdown."

Kara staggers out of the van and Lena climbs out after her with the help of her outstretched shaking hand. "Sub-level 19 ?" she asks the slight tremor in her voice sending uncontrollable shivers of fear through Lena. "Lockdown ?"

"I'm afraid we have no choice," J'onn replies gravely. "Sam's ETA is five minutes. We're closing down the moment she's in the building."

***

The ride down the sub-level 19 is nauseating, the elevator dropping like a sack of stones in water. Kara clings to the railing, and Lena clings to her.

Sub-level 19 turns out to be an almost mirror copy of command level. Screens line the far right wall and a large U-shaped console takes up the centre of the room. The high windows however are nowhere to be found replaced by a thick concrete wall, and where there should be doors leading to the maze of corridors, there are gaping holes covered by half lowered thick metal screens ready to be sealed. A large portion of the room is taken up by individual glass pods, fully equipped, and in one of them is Ruby.

The teenager is sitting prostrated on the ground, hand half extended towards the thick glass but not quite touching it. She raises her head at the sound of approaching footsteps but doesn't react much beyond that. Lena startles at the view, taking in her grey skin and chapped lips, and the thin trickle of hastily wiped blood under her nose.

Alex is crouching before her, leaning on the glass, looking small and frail, weaker than Lena has seen her in a long time. She too perks up at the newcomers and whirls around to launch herself at Kara. The Kryptonian staggers back but holds on, wrapping her arms against her and squeezing tight.

"You're here," Alex whispers, "you're here. How- ?"

Kara shrugs dismissively. "I’m a cyborg I suppose."

"Do you know where Sam is ? No one will tell me where Sam is ?!" Alex screeches, panic rising in her voice. "Ruby was cooking with Kelly, she fell from the countertop when it happened and I-"

"Breathe," Kara says, "breathe," she repeats. "Sam is on her way. She'll be here soon."

Sure enough, the elevator doors slide open and a gaggle of agents rushes inside, two of them pushing a gurney, and even from where she's standing, even without any supersenses, Lena can tell Sam is fairing far far worse than Kara is. She's been intubated, a third agent running alongside the gurney to pump air in her lungs and her face is a vibrant sickening lime green.

"We need a doctor in here ! She's flatlined !"

A gut wrenching scream ripples through the room and Alex tears herself out of her sister's arms to rush to Sam. She doesn't make it far, stopped halfway through by Kelly who bodily lifts her off the ground, bending back while she pins her arms to her side to keep her from escaping. Alex screams, the monosyllabic guttural sound ripping itself out of her throat to fill every nook and cranny of the room. She screams until it doesn't seem possible for her to produce any more sound and then screams some more before collapsing in a pile of limbs, dragging Kelly down with her.

"No no no please," Alex sobs on the ground. "Please... NO !"

The gurney is rolled into one of the air tight pods, Kara following suit because she's the only one strong enough to do CPR on Sam ; anyone else's arms would shatter on impact. She starts pushing on her chest, Lena counting in time with her because it's the only thing she can do as she stands there awkwardly, left behind by the rush of agents around her. The situation feels achingly familiar, she's been there before, the helpless one, and she feels her heart beating wildly in her chest, blood rushing to her ears and rendering her dizzy, useless.

Behind the thick glass, Kara becomes agitated and Lena realises she's left Sam's side and is mouthing something, words that remain caught on the other side of the barrier. Without her accord, Lena's eyes follow the direction she's pointing in, and land on the monitor she's hooked Sam to. She stumbles forward, her legs leadened, and manages to crouch down next to Alex. "There's a pulse," she says, her voice low and unsteady. "Sam has a pulse."

***

Things slow down to a sluggish almost stop. For now, not much more can be done ; at least not until the air in sub-level 19 has been pumped completely clean which is taking an awfully long time. Lena can't improve the system from down here, which is a grave design error in her humble opinion, but she's already thought of at least five different ways to do it. She could probably have thought of more, but the fact that the filtration system seems to be downright antiquated doesn't really help her concentrate.

She's sitting on the cold floor, back pressed to the thick glass panel of Sam's sealed chamber. They couldn't risk compromising her, and had to keep Kara in with her, turning her into a makeshift doctor with assistance from an actual doctor some forty floors up. She's stable for now, still intubated, her chest rising and falling mechanically ; but her skin is an unnatural colour, a mouldy green, and Lena can't help but think of some pistachios that would have been left out for too long. The first time this thought enters her mind, she has to hold back a hysterical laugh.

Each time Kara gets too close to Sam, adjusting her position or taking some measurements, a web of green veins spreads on her own skin. Lena knows, she thinks they all know, that her body must be working double time to keep the Kryptonite out, and that is not something that was taken into consideration when she worked on her code with Brainy. They should have thought of it, it appears obvious now, but in the heat of the moment, when all that mattered was preventing Kara from going on another rampage, it didn't even cross their minds. She prays, fully ready to convert herself to the first religion that will answer her wishes, that she doesn't have to regret it, that she doesn't have to live knowing she could have saved Kara and just forgot to do it.

She dozes off to the hum of the ventilation. She can't sleep, not when they are all still in danger, not when if she closes her eyes even for a minute, Sam might not wake up at all. A little further away, Alex is curled up on the floor, head pillowed on Kelly's lap, hand pressed to the wall of glass that separates her from her daughter, and Lena forces herself to look at her periodically to remind herself of all that there is to lose if she so much as take one wrong step.

Time passes by slowly, a dangerous lethargy taking hold of the room. Lena checks the clock a little after 1am, then again a little before 2, and finally, it's close to 3 when a loud clang fills the room, quickly followed by a creepy robotic voice that startles her out of her skin.

"Decontamination for subterranean levels 19, 18, 17, 16, 15, 14, and, 13, has been completed. No breach has been reported." The LED light that has been blinking on the control panel for the past hours flickers to green. "Decontamination will now proceed onto subterranean levels 12 to 1. To cancel the decontamination process please follow override protocol ORP-9."

Another loud clang resonates on the concrete walls but Lena already feels like she can breathe easier, her chest contracting with just a little less anguish.

"To unseal subterranean level 19 initiate protocol USP-S19," the announcement continues. "You now have ten seconds to initiate override protocol ORP-9. 9, 8, 7..."

J'onn unfolds himself from his cross-legged position on the floor and slowly makes his way to the control board. His lack of hurry makes Lena's own legs twitch. He looks down at the panel, nods to himself then claps his hands, the resulting sound causing everyone, even Lena, to snap to attention. The back of her head bumps painfully on the glass behind her.

"Doctor Veritas will be able to join us down here in two hours. We remain in lockdown for now until we can get a better grasp on the situation out there and figure out a way to clear the air planet wide. Agent Dox's latest analysis shows that Kryptonite concentration is at 37% right now therefore no Kryptonians will be allowed out of the building until further notice. We have managed to get a hold of Superman. He's been brought to his Fortress and is completely safe."

Lena's first reaction to this news is that she doesn't give a shit. The last time Superman crossed paths with one of them didn't end well for anyone, and one of Alex's fingers is still a little crooked as a result of trying to punch him. But if they got news from him, then, "can we communicate with the outside now ?" she blurts, "or did this come through the DEO's encrypted network ?"

This is a stupid side effect of their lockdown and she didn't exactly bother to hide her opinion about it earlier when she realised they were truly and well cut from everything. J'onn eyes her warily before answering. He's probably still expecting her to yell at him though Lena wouldn't fall this low ; she would use much more insidious boardroom-like tactics.

"Kryptonite concentration is at 41% and still rising," Brainy's voice says through the crackling comms.

J'onn sighs, wiping a weary hand on his face. "We have regained some communication capabilities and will be fully back online once we can unseal sub-level 1. In two hours. I'm afraid you will have to wait a little longer."

"We don't have 'a little longer'," Lena seethes, the determination she's trying to project severely undermined by the way her legs shake when she gathers them underneath her to push herself up. Behind the glass, Kara moves forward as if to support her. "We've already been down there for hours and Kryptonite levels are still rising outside. It's bound to be dangerous for humans too and you know it." She pauses for a second, staring at him in challenge.

"Listen," she continues, pleading," I know you're in a difficult position, I know there is no right call to make, but if I can access my private network, I can figure something out to get us out of this."

J'onn hesitates for a long moment, a multitude of feelings passing on his fatigued face. "There is a way," he says finally, "for you to reach ground level by manually unsealing sub-level 13."

"And you are not going to do it," Kara crackles through the speakers. "J'onn. Sub-level 12 is where we keep our most dangerous prisoners."

"I'll go with her."

Lena looks down, tracing the dusty concrete to where Alex is still lying on the floor.

"I'll go with her," Alex repeats, voice hoarse from all her crying. She pushes herself up with some difficulty, squeezing Kelly's hand before she lets go.

"Alex..."

"I have a big gun," Alex says, "and Lena can take care of herself."

"Reports show no sign of breach on sub-level 12," Brainy says, "the two of you should be fine."

In her glass cage, Kara frowns, a green shadow creasing her brow. Lena leans forward, pressing her hand to the glass. "I'll be back soon," she whispers, "I promise. Wait for me ?"

"You won't," J'onn interrupts with shitty timing, "you'll have to seal both sub-level 13 and 12 manually behind you and we won't be able to join you up until," he looks down out the control panel, "four hours when the full tower is decontaminated."

"Then I'll see you in four hours. Alex has my back, and I have hers," Lena whispers, "I promise. And I'm going to put an end to this. I love you, okay ?"

Kara sighs, letting her head fall on the glass on the other side of Lena's hand. "I love you."

"See you on the flip side," Alex mutters much more crassly ; and after Lena swipes a tablet out of an agent's bewildered hands, they cross the threshold of the first of many sealed doors.

***

They make their way through the first few levels in complete silence but for the sound of their shoes on the floor ; Alex's practical boots and Lena's ill-advised heels. The lights have been turned off to conserve power, and the glow of the red emergency lightning projects bloodcurdling shadows on the walls around them. Tension radiates from Alex and Lena isn't sure how to best approach the elephant in the room. She knows Alex isn't ready to talk about it, but the way things are going, she never will be.

"She," she starts at some point, quickly shutting her mouth and flattening herself against a wall when Alex requests her silence as they round a corner.

"You know," she attempts on another level before changing her mind and looking down at the tablet in her hands which is a bit too low on battery for her taste.

"I," she tries again just when they reach the sealed doors between sub-levels 13 and 12 ; but Alex fires her such an angry look that if she had heat vision like her sister, Lena would be ashes on the ground. It's like she knows what Lena wants to talk about, and is doing everything in her power to avoid it, short of silencing her permanently. Alex enters the manual override code with forced casualness and they step in yet another staircase ; the door sealing behind them has an air of finality.

Lena would very much like to never have to walk up another flight of stairs in her life ; unfortunately, they still have twelve more to climb, this one not included. It smells different here, acrid, like it did outside. She's breathless by the time they reach the next level ; Alex hasn't broken a sweat.

Sub-level 12 is creepy. The lights here are completely off, and the only thing counteracting the darkness is the blue glow emanating from the cells. She's never been on this level, though she has been invited to ; all she knows is that this is where they keep Brainiac's fried body because no one really knew what to do with it and they didn't want to take any chances.

Alex barely flinches when an alien throws themself at the glass when they walk by, she keeps walking confidently, her shoulders set. Lena pretends her stomach didn't just switch places with her heart.

Lena doesn't attempt to strike up a conversation again until they reach the last floor before ground level. Alex is busy unlocking the door, looking down at something on Lena's borrowed tablet.

"Sam is," Lena starts, tone unnaturally neutral. "She- She's going to be okay."

The tablet stumbles out of Alex's hand, hitting the floor with a dry sharp sound. Alex whirls around and stares at her, mouth parted soundlessly. They size each other up for a long moment, then Alex turns away from her again, and finishes unsealing the door.

"I'm in love with her," she whispers, her voice so small and broken that Lena doesn't know where to go from here. She knew, of course she did, but it's different to hear it aloud. "But I don't want to talk about it. Not now."

Before anything else can be said or done, the door slides open, and someone jumps into Lena's arms, sending her reeling a couple of steps back as she wavers on her heels.

"Thanks God you're here," Nia squeals loudly in her ear. "J'onn said you were coming up," she continues speaking much too quickly for Lena to process it, "but you took such a long time and I was getting worried and Brainy said not to worry but-" She releases Lena, briefly hugs Alex then, faced with her no-nonsense attitude, takes a couple of sheepish steps back. "What do you need ?"

"A computer and a lab," Lena says, dusting her hands on her unpractical dress. "And a change of clothes. I'm going to hack myself."

***

The hum of the ventilation is sickening. Lena can hear it clicking and clanging as it works double time to rid the DEO off all Kryptonite. Clearly, it wasn’t designed with that in mind. The entire tower has been sealed to the outside and the atmosphere up there is even more oppressive than down in the basement. Partly because it’s suppose to be daytime now, but no light is making it into the building, thick screen lowered over every window ; but mostly because Kara is forty floors down, sealed in a glass chamber with her infected best-friend and both of their fate resides on wether Lena can remove all trace of Kryptonite from the atmosphere and, frankly, she only has a vague idea of what to do.

The floor is cold beneath her feet, even through the thick soles of her borrowed boots and she shivers under her sweater and additional hoodie. She’s stopped short of slipping on some fingerless gloves but the AC does seem to be broken. It doesn’t seem to bother Alex who remains immobile in a corner of the lab. Then again, Alex could no doubt survive a nuclear winter with a t-shirt and a pocket knife, which now that Lena thinks about it, isn’t exactly a comforting thought.

Her fingers are fast on the keyboard. She’s already managed to extirpate herself from the complex security of the DEO’s private network to dive right into her own, trickier by some aspect, and she has to be careful now. She risks shutting herself out entirely if she isn’t and it would alert her entire security team. It seemed a good idea when she created it, but now all the firewalls and hidden switch are more of a nuisance. She takes a sip of the tomato soup Nia brought her up from the cafeteria ; it’s started to congeal and she almost spits it out. She forces herself to swallow, if only because she doesn’t want to ruin expensive lab equipment, enters a few more lines, presses the enter key with the carefulness she would have disarming a bomb and exhales longly when the screen reflects her computer’s desktop, the background a selfie she took with Kara and Krypto.

She activates her webcam then, as an afterthought, logs into the cameras surveying her office, just in case Eve walks in and she has to disconnect fast. She's ran several background checks on her new assistant, but she's not Jess. Suddenly feeling paranoid, she glances over her shoulder which is off course useless and doesn't assuage her nerves. Alex tries to soothe her with a smile but the resulting grimace has a radically opposite effect. She's just about ready to vibrate out of her own skin.

Scolding herself silently, she loads into her encrypted database, forcing her hands to steady so she doesn't mess up the 43 characters password that unlocks the biometric lock. Praying that the connection is stable enough, she highjacks her webcam to replace the feed with the DEO's and leans over the bulky computer to scan her retina. The screen fades to black and her heart misses a beat before a loading bar blinks into existence taking all the time she doesn't have to fill slowly.

Allowing herself a little gesture of impatience, she drums her finger against the table top and promptly stops when she almost knocks over the container of cold soup. Finally, the database finishes loading and an intense sense of relief washes over her when hundreds of files, unpatented projects, wishful notes and scribbles, blueprints and mechanical drawings. What she’s looking for however is not here.

Quietly, she swears under her breath. "Of course," she mumbles to herself, "of course."

Alex pops up behind her and this time, Lena swears loud enough to resonates in the small room.

"Of course what ?" Alex asks, nodding sharply.

"I'm not looking in the right place. I never moved Lex's files with my own."

"And can you access them ?"

Lena nods, takes a sip of the soup again then and swallows it with difficulty when she remembers it's inedible. "Might just take a few more minute. He had a dispersal device that I'd meant to reverse. The one I told you about. I have partial blueprints from a while back, but I never copied the file onto my own projects after he..."

"Do you just know everything your brother has ever worked on ?" Alex asks with a sliver of disbelief.

"Trauma will do that to you," Lena grumbles in reply before diving back into the database.

She's kept her files and Lex's separated, but she took the liberty of opening a backdoor, one that's well concealed, buried under lines of code, but that she finds easily anyway. At least this time, she had some foresight. She slips into his old files, shivering at the familiarity and at Alex's continued hawk-like presence over her shoulder. She scrolls through once, twice, thrice, but the device she's looking for simply isn't there. Files don't just disappear from encrypted databases, do they ?

It dawns on Lena, very slowly, too slowly really for someone of her intellect, that she checked her encrypted backdoor hadn't been touched, but she never looked at Lex's files after the hack happened. The last thing the screen displays before it fizzles to black, is a lime green message, "gotcha," followed by a winky face.

9. As long as it won’t separate you from me (Kara)

Summary for the Chapter:

In which Lena continues being an annoyed genius, Alex is the best person alive, and the situation temporarily goes from bad to worse.

Notes for the Chapter:

Title is from Separate by PVRIS, which might be the only PVRIS song on this playlist that isn't from Use me so enjoy ^^

It’s quiet. A little too quiet for Kara’s taste. She’s used to hearing everything, but with the DEO still on lockdown, no sound makes it in from the outside. So unused to having so little to tune out, her ears keep on focusing on every menial sound, the flow of her stupid IV drip, the electricity running through Sam's heart monitor, the heated tip of Lena's soldering iron. The hum of the sunlamps too, that they’ve turned up to eleven in the med bay.

Lena is frenzied in her work, but according to Alex, she’s calmed down considerably compared to when she found out what Lex did. She started by screaming insults at the top of her lungs for fifteen minutes, though Kara isn’t sure Alex isn’t exaggerating this one, then broke down in sobs and took a half an hour long shower. By the time Kara and the other were able to come up, she’d already printed her partial blueprint and was working her way up from there, hair held back in a ponytail so tight Kara worried for a moment that it was going to rip straight out of her skull.

Kara is supposed to be on bed rest, coddled, like the other Kryptonians, under heavy blankets, and hooked to all the monitors available in the DEO. But Lena needed her there and so she’s on chair rest, sitting next to her and offering her guidance in the form of little hums and onomatopoeias. She’s ripped off her oxygen mask a while ago but kept the IV ; Nia threatened to have her tied down in the med bay and she can be very scary when she wants to. Her threat was a bit negated by the hug she gave her after but like with most things, it’s the thought that counts. She got her soup too, tomato from the cafeteria, and she’s sipping it from a cardboard container, careful not to let even one drop fall on Lena’s work.

She’s never seen a device like that, something capable of ruining the entire atmosphere in less time than it takes to conjure up the thought and though she doesn’t doubt Lena’s smart, she struggles to see an exit to this situation. According to Brainy, Kryptonite levels are still rising outside, and she fears that she might never see the sun again, that she might never get out of here at all. She’s never been fond of being cooped up inside, and she’s even less fond of small spaces. It took everything she had earlier not to start screaming when she found herself locked in with Sam and the only reason she ultimately didn’t, the only way she managed to keep her cry locked inside of her, is that she knows they would have tried to get her out, and Sam would have died.

She's sleeping, knocked out by enough medicine to kill a horse. She's breathing on her own now, but every doctor they have available inside of the building is ready to intubate her again at a moment's notice. Alex hasn't moved from the med bay in hours, sitting perfectly still between her daughter and whoever Sam is to her. She fitted the breathing mask onto Ruby herself, brushing her hair away with an aching motherly tenderness. Ruby is faring better than her Yeyu, probably because she didn't fall from ten thousands feet but her skin is still tinged a pale greying green in places and her cheeks are flushed from a fever they're struggling to bring down. The machines they've been hooked to are working double time to pump the Kryptonite out of their systems but it's a slow work, and Kara prays they will hold on until they're both clean enough for their immune systems to kick in. She doesn't know what she would do if they didn't make it ; doesn't want to think about what would happen to Alex if they died.

Lena swears loudly as smoke starts billowing from her work table. Out of habit, Kara goes to breathe on it before it can get out of control but all she can manage is a weak cough. She wheezes, struggling to catch her breath, and sheepishly hands Lena a fire extinguisher, trying not to cower under her worried glare.

"Don't overexert yourself," she mumbles as she covers her entire table in white stinky foam. "I'm almost done."

"The whole thing did just catch on fire," Kara points out with maybe a little too much snark.

Lena whirls around, boots squeaking loudly on the concrete floor. "I'm doing my best," she snaps. "I know it's not much and I know it's my fault but I am doing my best."

All frustration evaporates from Kara instantly. "How is it your fault ?" she whispers. "How can you think that ?"

"How is it not ?" Lena bites back, "I should have checked his files and I didn't. If I had we wouldn't have been caught off guard, we would have had time to prepare, we would have-"

"You are not responsible for Lex's madness," Kara cuts, almost tripping over her IV in her hast to get closer. She manages to disentangle herself from the tube, wiggling pathetically for a moment before she can encase Lena in her arms. "You are doing your best, and your best is more than enough."

A minute comes and goes, a short moment during which a little bit of tension melts away from Lena and Kara manages to focus entirely on the beat of her heart. Then, Lena steps out of the embrace, straightens her sweatshirt and exhales slowly.

"Okay," she says, "okay. I’m good."

"Sure ?"

"As good as can be," Lena replies with a small shrug. She smiles weakly, a corner of her mouth tugging up briefly before her face settles back into a frown. "I just need to clean this up," she says, motioning to the crackling foam. "Make sure it's still working then reverse it and I was thinking of upgrading-"

She gets no chance to finish her sentence before the alarm starts blaring.

"Attention," a robotic voice sounds from all the speakers, "a breach has been reported on level 19. Attention..."

Lena blanches, her face paler than ever. "That's right below us. We need to, we need," she stammers, "get back downstairs and-"

Kara coughs. An invisible hand seizes her throat and squeezes, tight. "No," she manages, "no time. Seal the med bay."

"But you're not in the med bay," Lena says slowly.

"They need to seal the med bay !" she shouts, blood tearing itself out of her throat with her words.

She gurgles, the sound and sensation awful and familiar. With no warning, her knees shirk from under her and she hits the ground, the IV perch bending in two uselessly when she tries to hang onto it. She rolls over, flailing, as an intense burning licks at her veins.

She's going to die.

Her vision blurs, and she can barely see Lena dropping down next to her but she does feel her. She does feel her cool hands on her warm skin, the fingers that brush her hair away, the palm that rests on her sternum.

"It's going to kick in darling, you're going to be okay. You're going to be okay."

But her body doesn't kick in. Whatever saved her the first time isn't working now and she can't breathe she can't-

She claws at her face. There's something on it blocking her airways. Hands grasp her own and she tries to shake them away but she can’t, her own limbs too weak, too useless.

Hurried footsteps register distantly, she hears a scream, long and gutted, the sound of metal hitting flesh, and of flesh hitting metal.

The last thing she sees before she blacks out, is a green and purple android peering down on her.

The world sharpens again at whiplash speed. Fast enough in fact that when she opens her eyes, the android is still over her, with only the addition of an indent on the side of its head. Lena is standing next to it, what's left of the IV perch dented and raised over her head.

"Lex," she seethes, "I know it's you. Disarm your robot now or I will wreck it and use its part to impale you."

The android slowly turns to look at her, tilting its head to the side as the luminous slits that act as its eyes flicker. With a flick of its arm, Lena is sent flying like a pesky insect. Kara can hear the wind rushing out of her lungs when she makes contact with the wall.

In a blur, Kara is up, head-butting the android with all her remaining strength. She feels her own metal parts rattling on impact but her gesture still has the desired outcome and Lex's robotic goon crashes through the window and the railing and tumbles down, landing in a loud crash of metal and concrete.

Nia, who barely stepped out of the way, looks over the balustrade with caution and immediately steps back in horror ; a quarter of a second later, the android shoots up and over her head, flying straight to Kara. She barely dodges it but trips over her own feet in the process and hits the ground face first, taking down with herself Lena's work table and the precious device. As she eats a mouthful of concrete, she wonders what she's ever done to deserve such a thing. The answer is unfortunately obvious and as she rushes after the android to rip its processor out of its neck all she can think about is her own death, and everything that led to it.

The robot powers down pathetically, wiggling jerkily until it lays on the floor. Carefully, Kara toes at it for a moment, satisfied only when it doesn't move again.

"I thought Lex Luthor had been moved to a highly secure prison," Nia says, stepping in the lab through the broken window.

"Clearly," Lena replies drily, "it's not secure enough."

She gets up from where she landed, shaking the plaster from her clothes and hair and in a couple of quick strides is at her crushed work table to recover what can be salvaged. She stares intensely at her device, then, dimming it functioning, lays it down gently on the only upright tray in the room. She's less gentle when she snaps an oxygen mask on Kara's face.

"You keep that on now," she says. "And I need to work on a suit you can keep in your pocket. Something with anti-Kryptonite nanobots."

Frustration rising again, Kara thinks about protesting, but Lena swipes a tender thumb on her cheek, kisses the side of her head and whispers, low enough that she knows it's not meant for anyone but her, "I can't lose you again."

So Kara sits tight and waits patiently, a mere observer of Lena's work, a silent listener of Brainy's update. Alex sealed the med bay in time, and she managed to get Doctor Veritas in with her, just in case. J'onn phased through the breach to hold it and a couple of well trained agents are now patching it. Kryptonite levels outside have risen to 61%. There's a tightness in her chest, one that makes it hard to breathe, and she isn't sure it's entirely due to the Kryptonite. She's late for work. She falls asleep.

***

Kara doesn't wake up where she thinks she went to asleep. She remembers a hard chair digging into her back, a grey light, but the mattress that supports her back now definitely belongs to the med bay, and she can feel on her face the distinctive rays of a sunlamp. She opens one eye, then the other ; clean air trickles directly into her nostrils and she fights back a sneeze. A couple of steps away, Sam is awake, slurping spoonfuls of that Rao awful tomato soup that Nia must have brought her and that Kelly is now feeding her. On the other bed, Alex is reading a story to Ruby. Kara doesn't eavesdrop but by the way her face twists, she knows she's doing the voices. Lena is not there with them, but the med bay's door is open and she tracks her heartbeat a couple of rooms over in what is presumably a not destroyed laboratory. She wonders how long she's been asleep. She doesn't feel well rested, far from it. She feels battered and bruised and like an elephant has taken permanent residency on her chest, but at least, she's not alone.

Alex is the first one to notice she's awake ; she often is. She kisses the side of her daughter's head, smoothing a few errant strands of hair and pads to Kara's side. She hasn't slept, that much is clear, deep purple shadows carving caves under her bloodshot eyes. There's also a gash on her temple, hastily patched up with a couple of band aids. Kara points it out as soon as her sister gets close to her.

Alex waves it off. "It's nothing," she says, "I tripped on my way to the lockdown system."

"You nearly bashed your skull in is what you did," Sam grumbles from her bed. "It's a miracle you've made it this far in life."

"I could literally kill you with my pinky," Alex bites back with an unmistakable fondness.

"I'm sure you could," Sam replies, coughing on her soup. Out of the corner of her eye, Kara sees Kelly gently wiping a trickle of tomato from Sam's chin but she quickly averts her eyes ; this feels like something she shouldn't see.

"How are you feeling ?" Alex asks, nudging at her until she moves enough to clear a spot for her on the bed.

Kara pretends to think about it for a minute then says, rather drily, "like I went toe to toe with an angry robot while having Kryptonite poisoning."

Alex sighs. "I had this one coming." She remains silent for a moment, dabbing at Kara's forehead with a wet cloth. Kara lets her fuss ; that's how Alex reassures herself, by taking care of people. "Lena said you fell from pretty high," her sister eventually continues, her voice slightly strangled, "and J'onn said you almost died on the way here."

Kara shrugs, and regrets it immediately when the motion pulls at a wire plunged beneath her skin. "I'm okay."

"I'm scared."

This foreseeable confession hits Kara straight in the face. Of course her sister is scared ; she's only human. She's not this mystical invincible entity Kara likes to make of her, she's a person, and most everyone she loves almost died today.

"I know," she whispers, "but we're all here, and we're all going to be okay."

She's been lying too much lately for it not to come bite her in the ass soon.

***

After two full scans manage to convince Alex that she will be fine for the moment, Kara extricates herself from her bed and wires and, after a pit stop in the locker room for a shower and a change of clothe free of blood and vomit, she makes her way downstairs to the cafeteria in quest of not terrible food. She gets two large pizzas that she cleans out in a matter of minutes and a coffee that she knows Lena will appreciate, if only because it's warm and the AC is still working double time.

She finds Lena in a secondary, smaller, lab, hair in disarray, the sleeves of her borrowed hoodie rolled thrice over her forearms. She stops for a moment, leaning against the threshold, and looks at her. She hasn't slept either, looks at the end of her tether, but she's still working, hands picking at bits and pieces of metal, eyes focused on numbers too complicated and too small for her current state.

She notices Kara's arrival immediately, her heartbeat slowing down, and an invisible tension departing her shoulders, but she doesn't acknowledge her presence for another long minute as she finishes soldering two pieces of metal in what appears to be a box no larger than a smartphone.

"This is a prototype," she says eventually, looking up and motioning to the box. She's burnt the tip of her finger, and Kara superspeeds to her side to lay a cold kiss on it. "I still need to program the bots and I'm sure I can make it smaller but it'll do for now."

"What is it ?"

"A suit. For you. Don't get me wrong, your armour is great, but you need something that's a little bit more practical to carry around. This one has a built in foldable helmet and Kryptonite filtration." She speaks too fast for Kara to intervene, and when she seems to be done, takes a deep breath and adds in a slurred hurry, "so what do you think ?"

"I think you need to go to bed."

This, clearly, is not the reaction Lena expected, and her eyes widen as her bottom lip starts quivering.

"I'm sorry," Kara says, "this came out wrong. What I meant is that I think this is amazing, and I can never thank you enough for all the ways you've found of saving my life, but you're exhausted, and you need to sleep."

Lena sways a little, unsteady on her weary legs. "There is still so much to do," she whispers.

"And all of this will still be there for you to do once you've had a couple hours of sleep. You know you'll work better with a well rested brain."

"I know," she says, leaning in to rest her head on Kara's shoulder, "it's just..."

"Yeah, I know," Kara echoes. "Come on," she adds, swiftly picking Lena up in a bridal carry. "Let's get you to bed." Her own legs are still unsteady, but she manages to hide it well, probably because Lena has her eyes closed. "What's the status on the dispersal device ?"

Lena groans, pressing her face in the crook of Kara's shoulder. Her nose is cold, and her forehead much too warm. "I managed to reverse engineer it," she mumbles. "Brainy is setting it up right now and we should know if it's working within the next half hour or so. "At the current concentration of Kryptonite, it should take thirteen hours, seventeen minutes and eleven seconds to clean the entire atmosphere. Then the device will have to be encased in three layers of lead and buried. And I'll have to start from scratch for my CO2 cleaner."

"You can start from scratch tomorrow," Kara promises.

They've reached the med bay now, and she lays her down on the bed she vacated earlier. The moment Lena's head hits the pillow, she's out like a light.

She sleeps for a long time, and for the most part, Kara doesn't move from her side. She only leaves once, and only so Doctor Veritas can hook Lena up to some fluids and Alex can once more monitor her Kryptonite levels. Some time in the afternoon, she gets Brainy to bring her the android's head and a full set of tools so she can get a good look at it. She's not particularly thrilled about it, robots make her feel uncomfortable ; but it'll be one less thing on Lena's plate and a chance to maybe go home as soon as they can get out of here.

Later, J'onn returns to their side, and he brings with him a truck load of hot chocolate, cheap cookies and news from Eliza. The atmosphere in the med bay turns almost festive, especially since the blasting AC would make anyone believe it's winter. The radio however, isn't tuned on one of these frequencies that plays Christmas music throughout the year, but into the police scanner ; and while Alex and Ruby play a game of cards, Brainy is busy running an algorithm on all combinations of the name Lex, and its variable Alexander, and the surname Luthor. If he took the opportunity to escape, they'll be the first to know.

He hasn't so far which is maybe the most surprising and jarring thing that has happened in the past 24 hours. Kara would have thought it would be the perfect opportunity for him to just vanish, with all the Kryptonians incapacitated ; but apparently his prison really is highly secure. Or with all State agencies on the war path, he might just be biding his time. It makes Kara feel uncomfortable, queasy, and, guilty. Once again they are all in danger, and once again, it's because of her.

She's never going to know true lasting peace, is she ? There's always going to be something, someone, to put everything she cares about in jeopardy. She breaks everything she touches. Some days, her life feels like a big cosmic joke ; others, like today, Rao doesn't seem to care enough about her to give her even that.

Alex, sweet and caring Alex, the sibling she would have never dared to wish for, seems to pick up on her mood from across the room ; and once Kara is done hooking the robot to a tablet to run a scan on it, her and Ruby pack up their cards and come play with her. Somehow, Kara happens to win all the games, but Alex fervently denies any involvement in that, just like she always does.

Afternoon turns into night to the quiet sound of laughter. Or at least Kara supposes it does because they're still not allowed to open the thick metal screens separating them from the outside and her bed isn't angled in a way where she can see the clock. She's considering waking Lena up, though her sleeping schedule is already irremediably fucked up for at least the next few days, when she wakes up on her own, roused by the loud ding signalling that the scan is complete.

Lena stretches and yawns, scrunching her nose adorably, and together, they lean over the screen. Kara's heart drops to the bottom of her stomach. There's nothing on it but three little words, and a location tag, for L-Corp.

Notes for the Chapter:

I think this chapter marks the beginning of a weird obsession with tomato soup (unless I've mentioned it before and don't remember doing so), so I would like to state for the record that I do not dislike tomato soup. It is in fact part of this weird group of food that I could eat repeatedly and never get bored of, like plain pasta with cream and liquid strawberry-banana yoghurt (this is worded very weirdly but I do not put yoghurt in my pasta, I eat these separately, like a regular person).

10. For you I would breathe underwater (Lena)

Summary for the Chapter:

In which Lena continues to overwork herself, Kara tries to remain patient, and disaster takes the shape of a person.

Notes for the Chapter:

Title is from For You by Tonight Alive.

For anyone out there who's not Irish, which I'm going to assume is the majority of people reading this, Gardai are Irish cops (An Garda Síochána). It's roughly pronounced "gar-dee." If you're Irish and you're reading this, don't hate me, I've been to Ireland exactly once (😢).

There is a part in this chapter in which Lena refers to Alex as her sister. This refers to the end of Dreamboat when Alex and Lena dance at the wedding and Alex basically adopts her. It might be a little confusing if it's been a while since you've read it so I wanted to refresh your memory on that since it'll come up again.

/The sirens must be loud, Lena knows they must be because her home is right next to the Garda station and she hears them all the time. Right now however, she can't hear anything at all. Not even the words of the Garda leaning over her, his stale breath filling her little lungs like the water filled her Mum's. At least she figures this is what he must be explaining, that her mother drowned and isn't going to wake up.

The blanket they wrapped her in is itchy and it smells a bit like Seamus' poop. She wants to ask where her dog is, but her mouth refuses to produce any sound. She knows what happens to little kids who don't have parents anymore, and she isn't sure she'll be allowed to keep Seamus with her. Surely they can't take him away if this is all she has. Maybe if she asks nicely and leaves the rest of her things behind...

Closer to the edge of the lake, the Gardai become agitated ; they drag a limp shape out of the water. Sound returns all at once./

Lena's eyes fly open as a loud ding fills her ears. Her dream slips away from her grasp, and before she's fully processed that she's awake and has slept for far longer than she intended, she can't remember it at all. She yawns, stretches, and takes in Kara's tense form on the bed beside her. The offensive loud device is a tablet in her hands, and Lena wiggles ungracefully until she can peer at it. She promptly wishes she hadn't.

There's nothing on the screen but a short message, three little words, and a location, L-Corp.

Well done Lee.

It's not Lex, it's Mercy.

***

The hours that follow rank quite high amongst the worst moments of Lena’s life. Not, of course, as high as her mother’s death, not as high as her father’s funeral, and not even close to losing Kara ; but they still make it into her top ten easily. The wait is dreadful, and there is nothing they can do beyond passing all of their informations to the police. Lena can't be at L-Corp for damage control, no one can go out to help, they can't even open a goddamn window. Sam scares the shit out of everyone by falling asleep in the middle of a sentence, J'onn spends two hours on the phone with President Marsdin and Kara grows more and more angsty by the minute until she puts her hand straight through a table sending everything on it crashing loudly. She's kindly advised to go for a walk after that, but there isn't really anywhere to go.

Lena eventually drags her out of the room, on account that she needs to stretch her legs too. Really, she doesn't think she can handle seeing Mercy's joyful smile as she's dragged out of L-Corp one more time on the wide HD screen Brainy thought was a good idea to hook up in the med bay. She's also been around too many people for too long a time, and she needs her peace and quiet, even if that peace and quiet has to be found on the last floor of the DEO, cuddled to Kara on the cold emergency stairs that lead to the roof.

Once they are sure the air is clean, Kara will be the first one out of the building. Not that Lena thinks this is a particularly bright idea, but sometimes compromises have to be made, and she knows there is little Kara hates more than being cooped up inside. This is the primary reason Lena worked so fast, pushed herself so far even when she could barely stand on her own two feet anymore ; for Kara. Sure, she's also saving her best-friend and her niece in the process, and sending a big fuck you to her brother, and preventing a planet wide rise in lung cancer, but first and foremost, it's for Kara.

It’s always for Kara.

"Thank you," Kara says quietly.

"What for ?"

Lena realises, a little too late, that it sounds like she's fishing for compliments ; but if Kara notices, she doesn't say it.

"Everything," Kara replies, her voice still low and soothing and everything Lena needs right now. "Getting me out of there for starters."

Lena laughs, briefly, the sound a bit constrained and sad. "You were getting stir crazy," she says.

Kara laughs ; her laughter too is a bit restrained. "I was," she admits. "You always know what I need."

"I think maybe that's what I'm best at."

"You're good at a lot of things," Kara fires back, sounding somewhat aggravated on her behalf.

"Oh I know." With everything she's done today, and even if it doesn't feel like nearly enough, Lena knows selling herself short would be ill perceived, and maybe she does deserve to cut herself some slack. "I'm a certified genius. But there are some moments, when the most important thing is that I know you."

Kara presses a long kiss to the top of her head, lingers there and tightens her embrace. "Thank you," she says again.

In this single fleeting second, and despite everything, Lena feels safer than she ever has.

***

It's nighttime again by the time the lockdown is lifted and they're allowed out again, so much so that it could almost be the day before. Lena would like to pretend this day hasn't happened at all, that this was just a terrifying flourish of her imagination and it's the same night on the same roof ; but too much has changed in the past 24 hours, and this roof is too high up, this night too cold. The air smells different too, tastes almost too clean, like one's favourite sweater when it's been washed with the wrong detergent and has lost it's usual smell ; it's clean, but uncomfortably so, and though she tries not to, she can't help but fear that she's created a different problem. Kara doesn't say much, too absorbed in the flow of air in her lungs, but she exudes a quiet understanding that at least lets Lena know she isn't alone.

They don't really talk at all actually, apart from a couple of inquiries about Lena's comfort, if she's too cold or too tired, and she tries to enjoy this attempt at some peace and quiet until Kara straightens up and her head falls from her shoulder.

"Do you want to go home now ?" she asks with a certain hesitancy.

Lena catches everything there is in this question. Will they be safe home ? Will they manage to rest there ? Are they ready, most of all, to face whatever is out there, together ?

"No," she answers, stubborn in her need to be truthful, "but let's go anyway."

Alex insists on them taking a reinforced van home, Kara insists on flying them there, and on any other day, she would have won but tonight, with the memory of Kryptonite etched in her veins, the fall, Alex has little trouble convincing her. They end up in the back of a black windowless van much like the one that brought them here, if for the fact that this one has seats and, for some strange reason, a minibar that Lena struggles not to get into. The lack of windows is a curse for the entire ride, Lena not being as good as Kara at knowing where she is simply based on the turns the vehicle makes. It becomes a blessing the moment the car turns into their street. 

She can hear them even through the thick Nth metals ; reporters. 

The van covers the last few meters sluggishly, caught in what Lena pictures to be a tidal wave of angry journalists, and if she didn’t want to be home so much, they’d be on their way to a safe house right now. She’s got access to one in most countries, curtesy of Lex’s rampant paranoia ; and some of them not even him knows about, curtesy of hers. She thinks it would break her though, to run away now, to admit defeat in a game that’s barely just began, and this is why she allows Kara to help her out of the car and shield her all the way to the building. She notices two more guards in the hallway, and no matter how hard she tries, no matter how hard she presses her face in the crook of Kara’s neck, she can’t pretend she didn’t see them, can’t pretend she doesn’t know her own brother wants her dead, can't pretend the one board member she thought she could trust turned out to be one of his pawn after all.

Kara is talking to her when they enter their apartment but she doesn't really register what she's saying, to focused on the rise and fall of her voice to notice anything else. She chooses to believe she's speaking soft reassurances, even if when she turns to look at her, she sees her activating the lockdown system, a state of the art security panel hidden behind a horrendous tacky print. Someone took care of Krypto while they were away, and they won't have to come out again until morning ; the prospect is truly terrifying. Now that they're home, just the two of them, the hours that stretch until the next day seem insurmountable to Lena. She doesn't know how to occupy them, fears she won't even be able to fall asleep to pass the time.

Kara silently retreats to the bathroom, head low and shoulders hunched. For a splint second, Lena wants to follow her, wants to press her up against the patched up tiles of their shower and forget that the past 24 hours ever existed. But for the first time in a long time, the desire to be on her own, to close in on herself and to keep even Kara away, is stronger, and she stays back, frozen to the spot for a long minute after her girlfriend disappears through the door.

She's wishing for a respite, but she doesn't get it, and as soon as the shower starts running, her body switches to autopilot, taking her around the room in a frenzy of motions. She knows, or at least part of her does, that cleaning her apartment won't miraculously fix her life, but when nothing is going right, she can't bear anything being out of place and there's a stain on the counter that just won't come off and her hands are sticky and gross, her hair clings to the sweat on her neck and-

"Lena ?"

Kara materialises behind her ; and the sudden presence when there was no one just a second before has Lena startling, only Kara's quick reflexes saving her from splitting her forehead open on the ajar door of a cupboard. A door that shouldn't have been opened in the first place, a door that would have been closed if Lena had been paying attention, if she'd been better at what she does, less stupid less fucked up less-

"Come take a bath with me ?"

"I can't," Lena snaps immediately, the act of speaking hurting her clenched jaw. "There is..." She motions around, her arm feeling alien to herself. "There is... There's so much to do." She waves around again, hoping that Kara will understand. Or will take her out of the hole she's dug for herself. Anything, she will take anything.

A heavy, grounding, hand falls on her shoulder and for a split second, she can breathe right again.

"Okay," Kara says, "okay. Where do you need me ? What can I do to help ?"

The questions stun her. This is what she wanted and yet now that Kara's offered it, she doesn't know what to do.

"Tell you what," Kara continues, her hand sliding down her arm to grab her clammy disgusting palm, "I can finish cleaning this up for you, do the dishes, and you can go take a shower. I'll be here when you're done, I promise."

Lena looks down at her hands, checking that they're still here, that they're still hers. They're raw and red from all the scrubbing and her skin crawls at the thought of how filthy she must be.

"Okay," she whispers.

"Okay ?"

Lena nods, her head bouncing up and down with a little too much vigour. "I'll go take a shower."

Kara drops her hand, steps back to let her move away and something about it feels intensely wrong. But it's all in her head, it's her mind lying to her and she knows it because Kara leans in to kiss her sweetly on the cheek like she always does and everything is going to be okay.

She walks to the bathroom and, driven by a pull she can't ignore, turns to look at her love before she closes the door. She whirls around just in time to see her shoulders drop with something not dissimilar to defeat as Kara picks up the sponge and starts wiping the countertop. The impression that something is amiss comes back tenfold.

***

Sam sighs, and Lena echoes her sigh, dragging it as long as she can. She thinks about Kara, warm in bed this morning, and how hard it was to leave her. She wishes they'd both taken the day off, but knows then can't. Her palms are clammy again, and she wipes them on her slacks, peering at the fabric intensely as she does so.

"We need to find her a replacement," Sam says, "no matter how temporary."

"I know that," Lena seethes. "She may have played me, us, but we can't let her shares fall into the hands of those who will not even pretend."

"So," Sam pushes closer the pictures Lena has been wholly ignoring since the beginning of their meeting, "who's going to be your placeholder for the time being ? Young and inexperienced Alia Keralis, who sure, is a genius, but that prerequisite isn't actually required to sit on a board, or," Lena can see where this is going from a mile away, "battle hardened Andrea Rojas who basically grew up in a board room but is a 'bad idea for obvious reasons' ?"

Lena sighs, the answer to her conundrum is rather obvious, and she knows if she were to call Andrea, she would pick up in a second, even if they didn’t exactly part on good terms, but she just can’t.

"Or," Sam continues with a somber look, "we can let Mercy's shares of the company go to the wolves. Watching old white men fighting each other might be entertaining after all."

"What about Bruce ?"

"Do you really want Wayne Industries to have a say in what L-Corp does ?" Sam asks dryly.

"No," Lena mumbles in defeat, shoulders dropping in what is certainly not worthy of a renown CEO.

"I can even talk to Andy for you. I've always dreamed of having a word with the woman who fucked my best friend so much the next woman she ended up with was a manipulative bitch."

"You will do no such thing," Lena bites, trying to infuse steel in her tone, "we don’t need a repeat of last time. I will draft a proposal and will have Eve call both Andrea Rojas and Alia Keralis so I can make an informed decision."

She casts a glance to the tower of rejected files. She shouldn't be surprised that so little people made the cut of her background checks but still, she can't possibly offer shares of her company to her bloody ex. Andrea might be a ruthless and talented business woman, but to Lena, she will always be the serial cheater who quite literally fled their relationship and sent her a wedding invite. She doesn't exactly see her as trustworthy.

"I need to get going, I have," Sam says, marking a bizarre pause, "lunch."

"Lunch ?" Lena echoes. She glances down at her watch, it's barely eleven.

Sam nods. She's already out of her chair and gathering her bag before Lena can question her further. "Think about it," she says just as the door swings shut behind her.

Lena spends much too long, after Sam's departure, looking at the opened files before her. If she does nothing, there is a risk her company will tank, possibly irremediably. Getting L-Corp out of Lex's shadow was already a lot of work the first time, she doesn't know if she can do it twice, especially since having let one of his minion operate right under her nose doesn't bode well at all for her reputation. Which, fuck, reminds her she needs to schedule a press conference, or at the very least an interview, which means someone is bound to try to kill her again very soon.

She's still mulling over her impossible decision when Kara touches down on her balcony for their own lunch.

"Did someone order a Super-delivery ?" she asks, grinning and shaking the two take-out bags she's holding.

To Lena, her arrival is a gulp of fresh air, a hand reaching out to drag her to the surface. With Kara, for Kara, she can do anything. She glances down at the pictures again, selects one and puts the other on the rejection pile. Now all she needs to do, is make a convincing proposal.

***

The weeks that follow the Kryptonite storm are dreadful. A cloud of anxiety descends on Lena and no matter which direction she chooses, it never seems to clear up, anguish squeezing at her chest at every waking moment. Every second spent away from Kara is a second where it's hard to breathe, but Kara's presence doesn't abate the fear as much as it should. Even when she's around her, the hand that has burrowed itself inside of Lena remains tightly wrapped around her heart and she knows, she just knows, that something terrible is going to happen ; it’s only a matter of when.

Kara for her part remains equal to herself. Strong, steady, warm, absolutely terrified of sleeping alone at night. It hasn't really been a problem until now, except maybe when Lena gets up to go to the bathroom and comes back to find Kara fighting the bed sheets ; and it wouldn't be a problem now, if she weren't pulling so many late nights. She knows that she doesn't need to fix everything by herself, knows that she doesn't have to double check all of the mess Mercy left behind her ; except that she kind of has to, because who can she trust at L-Corp now but Sam, and maybe Jack ?

It's harrowing, working so much, spending so much time away from her family, fixing things and making sure the things that are right don't need to be fixed. But every time she comes home late to find Kara sprawled on the couch with Krypto, dinner cooling on the table, every minute she stays at work, every second, is the thing that could save her. It doesn't make it less terrible, but it makes it worth it.

"I worry about her," she hears Kara say through the door one night as she comes in a little before eleven.

She stops, keys clutched in one hand, bag heavy in the crook of her elbow. Kara must have heard her coming, right ? She always does.

Kara however, shows no sign that she's heard Lena behind the door, and continues. "I understand why she's doing what she's doing. She's scared, she feels responsible, and I can make compromises. If she can't be home for dinner, I can drop by with some food, if she needs space, I can give her space. I know I'm being a little bit too clingy, but she's overworking herself and I worry."

There is a pause in the conversation, and Lena figures whoever is on the other side of the phone must be agreeing, but it's from the inside of the apartment that an answer comes and she realises Alex is here with her.

"It's okay if you're disappointed," she says, and Lena's heart drops to the bottom of her stomach. "Just because you know she has a tendency to lock herself in her own head doesn’t mean you can’t be disappointed that she's doing it."

"I'm not disappointed," Kara says immediately. Lena can picture perfectly the way her brow must have furrowed at the implication.

"But you are," Alex says softly. "Stop moving," she adds grumpily and Lena finally hears the faint sound of the clipper. This must be why Kara hasn't heard her.

"I just worry she's going to hurt herself." Kara sighs, marks a long pause ; Lena braces herself for what's coming. "And yeah," she adds, "she's never home anymore. And it's not just me, right ? I'm not being selfish ? She also missed her therapy appointment twice in the past few weeks, cancelled on you, cancelled on Jack..."

"It's not just you," Alex reassures softly. "Maybe try to talk to her about it ? It worked last time."

Kara sighs and Lena can hear her perfectly ; they might need to change the door if it's flimsy enough that she can perceive everything happening inside their home. The buzzing of the clipper changes minutely, Alex must be putting the finishing touches to the back of Kara's head. Purposefully, Lena drops the keys and swears loudly and a little artificially, before bending down to retrieve them. She jingles them excessively when she shoves them into the lock, and apparently makes enough noise that when she finally shoulders the door open and stumbles inside, the two occupants of the apartment are sharing concerned looks. She thinks about apologising, for the noise and for being home late, but her excuses die on the tip of her tongue at the look on Kara’s face when she gets up from her position on a floor and brushes stray hair from her sweatpants.

"I made pasta," she says wearily, "and mushroom sauce, but I’m afraid it’s all jellied by now." She scratches the back of her head where her hair is short and soft and adds, pensively, "it might be good if I pop it in the microwave though. Do you want to take a shower first, or are you hungry ?"

Lena, to everyone’s surprise including her own, bursts into tears ; and once she's started, she can't stop.

She's vaguely aware that she's babbling some sort of messed up apology, words fleeing her mouth almost as fast as the snot dripping from her nose. Someone is rubbing a comforting hand down her back, Alex she reckons, since Kara is crouching in front of her, her look of concern slightly blurry through Lena's tears.

"I'm a terrible person," she sputters, gooey salt coating the inside of her mouth, "a terrible terrible person."

"No you're not !" the sisters cut in tandem. A flicker of something crosses Kara's face, and she hopes to God it's not pity.

"I heard you," Lena babbles on, distantly aware that she previously had no intention of disclosing that fact. "I hurt people, I hurt you. It's all I'm good at. And what for ?" She coughs, half-chokes and stammers ungracefully. Alex's hand presses harder against her back, in an effort, she supposes, to ground her. "L-Corp is still going down, I've got nothing but bad reviews, I'm going to lose everything."

"I’m sorry," Kara says, "I tried to block that article but..."

"Now you're just being dramatic," Alex says in her ear, and Krypto seems to agree because he whines and presses his head on her lap.

Lena snorts with a distinct lack of grace. "You don't understand."

"Explain it to me then," Alex says, "to Kara."

"L-Corp hasn't been doing good for a while," she whispers. "A lot of major investors pulled away and Mercy might have been a soulless betraying cunt but she was a supportive one and now that all of her assets have been frozen I need to find someone to inject money in the company."

She wipes her eyes, smudging her clearly not waterproof mascara on her hand. Kara takes that hand before she can squeeze it back against her chest and kisses her knuckles with care, like Lena has never done anything bad in her life.

"If L-Corp falls," she continues, clearing her throat and threading her fingers with Kara's, "I fall. And if I fall, I can't protect you anymore."

"It's-" Kara starts.

"It's not okay Kara and you know it."

"That's not what I was going to say," Kara continues, taking hold of her second hand. She nods to her sister, and Alex rises, mumbling something about making some tea."I was going to say that it sucks, big time," she stops to search for Lena's eyes, offering a tentative grin, "but that you don't have to do it all on your own. You don't have to hold your breath because you think you can save everyone that way. We're here for you. Sam and Jack at L-Corp are here for you. Let them help. Let me help. You hurting yourself is not going to fix anything."

Lena coughs again, and Krypto raises his head to look at her with big sad eyes. The loss of warmth on her lap startles her momentarily but she shakes it off. She needs to be stronger than that. "I'm doing it for you," she says, trying, and failing, to project aplomb and strength.

"But I don't want you to do that, I've never wanted you to do that." Kara speaks softly, but her words are like a slap to Lena's face. "We do things together. We're partners. You can't constantly sacrifice yourself for me, just like I can't give away all of myself for you. But you do give me strength, you do lift me up every time I need it ; let me do that again for you."

"You've always been better at that than me," Lena mumbles self-deprecatingly.

"I'm not," Kara says, kissing her hand again, then her forehead, "we all lose perspective once in a while."

Alex plops down on the floor next to them and Kara liberates her hands so she can grab the mugs. She frowns. "The blue one's decaf, right ?"

Lena nods, and the process sparks the beginning of a pounding headache. "Thank you," she manages to say crookedly.

"Anytime," her sister says, kissing the side of her head. She smells like Sam's shampoo. "I’m going to go. Are the two of you going to be okay on your own ?"

Lena looks up at Kara, searching for the right answer on her face, but Alex is looking at her and so she nods again. "We will," she croaks, taking a sip of her light tea. "Thank you."

Alex kisses the side of her head again, then Kara's, and pats Krypto before rising fluidly and making a beeline for the door where she stops briefly to slip on her shoes. "I'll come by for coffee tomorrow," she says, before the door can close behind her.

Lena has a million things to do tomorrow, but she'll clear her schedule ; she'll do anything.

"Do you want to take a shower ?" Kara asks once they're alone.

"With you ?"

"If you want."

Kara gets up in one precise motion, her body cutting a clean line in front of Lena. She helps her up too, her arm steady under her grip, and before she can take a step back, Lena buries herself in her embrace. "I’m sorry," she says.

"It's okay," Kara whispers. "I promise you it's okay. Just don't shut me out. I can be your strength if you need me to be, but please, don't shut me out."

A silent tear rolls down Lena's face and disappears in the checkered fabric of Kara's cozy shirt. She presses harder against her, trying to borrow some of that strength Kara offered. She would do impossible things for her ; she will if she has to.

***

Lena stares at the article laying on her desk, disgruntled that the coffee mug she set on it warped and stained the newspaper. The title stares right back at her. WHY L-CORP IS THE COMPANY WE NEED RIGHT NOW, by Kara Danvers. She wonders how much trouble Kara went to for it, how many favours she had to pull to be able to write an article about her girlfriend. Maybe none, maybe it's just a privilege that comes with being Supergirl. Either way, she appreciates that Kara just did it, that she went and deconstructed every bad article written about her and L-Corp since Mercy's fall and turned them into one glowing review, illustrated by a picture of her laughing in the middle of her interns. There's bound to be backlash, there always is, but right now it's exactly what she needed to read, and she understand why Kara carefully folded the newspaper in her briefcase along with some of her favourite mint flavoured dark chocolate before she flew off this morning.

She takes a sip of her coffee. It's a little bit too bitter but it's the only drink she can entrust Eve with ; she asked her for tea once, and ended up with half brewed Yellow Lipton. Shuffling her papers, she extracts a file from under Kara's article, and opens it. There's a contract inside, and all the documents she needs to transfer Mercy's shares to her new board member ; if her new board member bothers turning up for their meeting. Lena still half hopes that she won't, but steels herself when Eve's voice crackles through the intercom.

"Miss Luthor ? Your 2 o'clock is here."

Lena shoves the article back into her briefcase then dusts her desk, putting the crumbs from the granola bar she ate for lunch in her wastebasket. She straightens her jacket, pushes a few strands of hair behind her ears then feels ridiculous for doing so and says, "bring her in."

The door opens immediately and through it walks Andrea Rojas.

Notes for the Chapter:

I've never drank decaf tea but it's definitely a thing since they sell it on Barry's tea's website. I have no idea if it's good or not, it might be terrible, if you try it and it kills you, I will not be held responsible.

11. They all warned us about times like this (Kara)

Summary for the Chapter:

In which Lena learns something surprising about her mother, that one coworker is an asshole, and it all goes downhill from here (but at least Lena is not wearing a bra so there's a silver lining).

Notes for the Chapter:

Title is from False God by Taylor Swift, and yes, I am deeply sorry.

Content warning : Lillian is in this chapter so there will be some discussion of cancer and hospitals.

Kara makes her way through traffic slowly, one hand on the wheel, the other on Lena's thigh, her thumb swiping on the fabric of her slacks as much for Lena’s comfort as for her own. Today's situation is not ideal, but she loves little moments like this one, moments when they feel like real people, and not like two giants, much too big for the world they live in. Lena tenses when they turn into the underground parking lot of the hospital and leave the bright light of the street for the dark shadows of a low concrete ceiling. She's been tensed a lot lately, but she's trying, which is all Kara asks for. She's home most nights of the week again, passed some of her work load to her collaborators, and the recent arrival of a new member on her board, allowed her to flip it in her favour to release early the smallest kinetic battery known to humankind which in turn, brought L-Corp stocks' up again. Things might not be going great, but they are going better.

"You still have time to change your mind," Kara says as she pulls up into a spot exactly halfway between the exit and the elevator. She loathes underground parkings, and so does Lena, but she's mapped out all seven ways out of this place, not counting busting through the ceiling, and it helps steady the trembling of her leg.

Lena sighs, presses her palms on her eyes then undoes her seatbelt. "I've missed all of her previous sessions already," she says, "I need to go to this one. And if that's still okay with you, I'd rather you stay with me."

"Of course," Kara says, rounding the car in a flash to open her door, "anything you need. Ready ?"

Lena shakes her head softly, pushes a strand of hair behind her ear and adjusts the bracelet on her wrist. "Yeah."

They make their way up to the cancer aisle through a large and sanitised elevator, the clean and nauseating hospital smell assaulting Kara's nose before they're even in it. Lillian Luthor has been given a private room for her chemotherapy, a wide space of pale green walls and squeaking grey linoleum with soft classical music wafting through it. Kara remembers Alex's grand-father needing chemo for his cancer, she remembers a crowded room with plastic curtains, piss yellow walls and a distinctive stench of illness ; he'd been given no special treatment, even with Eliza's position at the hospital.

"Good afternoon," Lillian says pleasantly when they make their way inside, "Lena, Kara."

"Kara is non negotiable," Lena says in lieu of a reply.

"Of course she isn't dear. Come sit, both of you. Do you want anything to drink ? I can have something brought up from the cafeteria, their coffee is surprisingly decent."

"I'll take a coffee, thank you," Lena replies, sitting very properly on the plastic chair closest to Lillian. "Kara ?"

"Coffee sounds nice," Kara says a little hesitantly. She has absolutely no idea of how to navigate this stilted and awkward situation. She knows Lena and her mother have never been close but they sound so hollow and contrived that she could think she'd just walk onto the set of a poorly acted play.

She ducks her head in her coffee the moment it’s brought to her, the bitter smell covering for a moment the sharp and tang scent of the chemicals coursing through Lillian. "Won't the smell bother you ?" she asks, quite suddenly if she's to believe the twin looks of surprise on the Luthor women's faces. "Of the coffee ?" she then elaborates, lifting her cardboard cup.

"Oh no," Lillian dismisses with practised carelessness, "I can't really smell or taste coffee anymore. Which is a shame really, I rather enjoyed these little unhealthy sugary squash latte."

"Pumpkin spice latte ?" Lena tries tentatively.

Lillian waves her hand, "yes," she says, "this one. It was my favourite."

Kara watches as Lena looks at Lillian with wide eyes, seemingly seeing her mother for the first time. "Pumpkin spice," she repeats under her breath, bewildered.

"I'm sure I can figure something out," she then adds, louder. "I have an employee who wrote one of his thesis on the side effects of chemotherapy and how to counteract them with alternative treatments." She pauses, then says, "it’s Jack," for Kara’s benefit. "He's working on nanobots now but if I switch his team with-"

"You will do no such thing," Lillian cuts, "L-Corp cannot spare the funding."

"And you," Lena seethes, "will not tell me what I can and cannot do."

Lillian blinks, winces. "That's fair," she says. "I'm sorry."

"So," Lena continues, abandoning her coffee to whip out a tablet out of her handbag, "describe your symptoms for me."

"You work too much," Lillian sighs, and Kara is inclined to agree even if she won't side with her in front of Lena. "And you're not a doctor."

"I have three PhDs," Lena interrupts dryly.

"You are not that kind of doctor then," Lillian corrects. "I promise I will send you a complete lists of my symptoms and you can put someone on my case, anonymously of course, but today I thought we could talk about something else."

"And what exactly are we supposed to talk about ? The weather ?"

"Well yes," Lillian says calmly, "tell me about that device of yours, the one you're working on to clear our atmosphere of harmful gases." She nods towards Kara then adds, "I read all about it in that brilliant article in The Tribune."

Lena stares at her mother for a long moment, rendered completely speechless. Discreetly, or at least she intends to be and then her chair screeches loudly on the floor, Kara gets closer to her and puts a gentle hand on her back. Lena takes a long sip of her coffee, then looks up at Lillian with a strange expression in her eyes. Kara thinks she's not going to speak, fears she might even walk out, but she doesn't, and soon, the room is filled with the passionate lilt of her voice as she launches in a description of her latest work.

They stay until the end of Lillian's session, after what they step outside to give her a modicum of privacy. Lena is silent as she leans against Kara in the hallway, but she's no longer tensed, bear herself differently, like a physical weight has been lifted off her chest.

"You good ?" Kara asks, kissing her shoulder just where her blouse gives way to skin.

Lena hums in reply, snuggling closer with no concern for the busy corridor. "I'm okay," she then says, "I wasn't sure how it would go but..."

"It went well ?"

Lena nods. "Yeah. Yeah it went well. This is surprising."

"But good."

"But good," Lena confirms.

Lillian chooses this moment, when Kara knows Lena is about to turn in her arms to kiss her, to exit her room, prime and proper as ever, but a little frail looking. She, in Kara's opinion, looks like fancy paper getting tossed around by the wind. She hovers awkwardly on the threshold, then buries herself in her purse to dig around for her phone and extracts it with clumsy triumph.

"Are you ready to get home ?" Lena asks.

"Yes. I just need to let my driver know he can pick me up and-"

"We could drive you home," Lena offers quickly, rushing her words out before she can regret them.

She turns to Kara questioningly and Kara nods. "We can," she agrees, "if you want."

Lillian ponders over it for a long moment, thumb suspended over her phone, half ready to text her driver. She turns to Lena, her face unreadable and smoothed over to hide any and all emotions. "If you don't mind."

Kara rushes down to the parking lot to get the car and meet them out front where she finds them standing stiff and silent again, Lena looking down at her phone and Lillian fixated on a bird in a tree across the street. The radio saves them from a completely quiet ride, but by the time they reach Lillian's penthouse, the atmosphere is tense enough that Kara wonders if all the benefit they ripped from these two hours have simply evaporated while she had her back turned. She cuts the engine, plunging them into silence, and clears her throat.

"Thank you," Lillian says after a moment, "it was lovely to have you with me today, both of you. I am quite tired," she stops to look at Lena, inhales sharply then continues, "but I would love to have you over for tea some other time. If you still like tea."

"I do," Lena replies, "still like tea. And it would be lovely," she says, echoing Lillian's earlier words.

"Great, then it's settled. Let me know when you're free ?"

"I will."

"Thank you," Lillian says again. A second passes, she reaches across the seat to briefly squeeze Lena's shoulder and then, she exits the car, silently closing the door behind her.
