She does pause to wait for her which gives Alex the opportunity to catch up and before Lena can say or do anything, Kara's broad frame is tucked neatly and safely in her sister's arms. Alex whispers something that Lena doesn't hear to which Kara nods weakly and then, it's just the two of them again.

They ride home in complete silence ; so much so that the agent driving their bulletproof van feels the need to turn on the radio. At least Kara is touching her again, holding her hand in a strange artificial grasp that doesn't exactly make her feel better. Lena tentatively leans in just before the car turns in their street and wonders if this is what it's like to miss someone who's right there. The worst, she thinks, is not knowing what's going on inside of Kara's mind, not knowing why she's been frozen out and left on the side of the road. She can guess, but her own mind has been known for going a little overboard from time to time and she doesn't want to panic unless it's absolutely necessary.

Kara retrieves their mail with more force than is necessary, denting the box in the process, then stalks upstairs heavily, the steps creaking dangerously under her weight. Lena hurries after her, her name ready to tumble off her lips but before she can say or do anything, Kara loudly announces she's going to bed, and disappears from sight, barely stopping to greet Krypto when he barrels into her. Lena is ready to go after her but stops halfway through taking a step, instead remaining where she is to pet Krypto in the doorway. Maybe Kara just needs time, maybe everything will be alright again if she just lets the night pass.

In the meantime, she busies herself as best as she can, cleaning the kitchen and then taking a long shower, staying under the stream until the water turns tepid and disagreeable. Only then does she turn up to bed, slipping in the cold sheets beside Kara while Krypto settles at the foot of the mattress, sure to be a tripping hazard come morning.

Kara is not asleep, and usually, she would roll to her side to gather Lena in her arms, tucking her tight against her body until their limbs would be indistinguishable from one another. This time, she doesn't, this time, she remains still and stiff on her back, as far away as the edge of the bed allows. Lena tries to keep quiet, bites back a sob, but quite honestly, it's been a very long 24 hours, and she just wants a hug. A tear that she wills to be silent rolls down her cheek but a gasp breaks through nonetheless and she rolls into a ball, trying to keep quiet.

This seems to be what gets to Kara and finally, finally, she shuffles closer and wraps an arm tight around her, tugging until Lena unwinds and glues herself to her, hands clutching at the soft fabric of her shirt. The embrace is still tense, Kara's body rigid against hers, but at least, she's warm again.

"I'm sorry," Kara says, so low that at first Lena isn't sure she really heard her speak. "I'm sorry," she says again. "I'm trying to process everything, but I'm not doing great. I'm not angry at you, I'm just upset and I'm trying very hard not to be."

"I'm sorry too," Lena whispers.

"Do you know what you're apologising for ?" Kara asks, drawing back a little to look at her, eyes piercing even in the darkness of the room.

"I should have kept better tabs on Lex and-"

"This is not about Lex," Kara cuts softly. "Listen, I'm trying not to make a big deal out of this, I'll feel better in the morning."

"But I made it a big deal in the first place," Lena says, realisation dawning on her, "by not telling you about it."

"Yeah," Kara breathes. "I'm trying not to make a mountain out of it, especially with everything else that's going on, but just- It's hard for me to believe that there's nothing going on there when you went to such great length to hide it from me."

"I didn't want to hide it from you," Lena says quickly. "I just didn't know how to tell you. And I wanted to. So bad. But Andrea's always going to be a sore subject for me and I just didn't know how to."

"I don't understand," Kara says, "why of all the atrocities that have happened in your life and mine, this is the thing that you would keep from me. Don't get me wrong. You're entitled to your privacy, you're allowed to keep things to yourself, this is not what I want from you. But it's hard not to see this as a big deal."

"Can I try to explain it to you now ?" Lena asks. "If it's not too late ?"

Tenderly, Kara kisses the crown of her head. "It's never going to be too late for you and me."

"Andrea and I have a complex history," Lena begins, chuckling sadly at her choice of words, "and I think over the years I've started to see her as a catalyst for a lot of things  in my life. Rarely good ones. I don't think I would have tried so hard to mould myself into what Veronica wanted if not for Andrea."

"What happened with Veronica was not your fault," Kara interrupts gently.

"Andrea left me a lot. Came back a lot too. She strung me along for a long time and well, I let her. I was never the best version of myself when I was with her, but she was at her best with me." Lena pauses here to clear her throat, annoyed that it keeps on cracking weakly. "And then one day she left for good. She left a note on my bedside table, packed her bags and vanished. I tried to go after her, but turns out TSA doesn't care about your big romantic gestures. She didn't even look back anyway. It took me a while to stop caring, to build myself back up and decide I was better on my own. Sam helped a lot. And then, one day, I received a wedding invite. No context, no explanation, just an invitation to her fucking wedding."

Lena breathes in and out slowly, taking a second to clear her mind before she gets angry. "She showed up on my doorstep six months later with a big ugly diamond on her finger and an apology. Sam is the one who opened the door, and I didn't hear from her again until I contacted her myself for L-Corp's sake."

Silence follows her words, and she doesn't attempt to fill it, intent on giving Kara enough space to think about it.

"Okay," Kara says eventually. "Thank you. For telling me. She still," she clears her throat loudly, "she still cares about you a lot."

"We're always going to have history, I can't deny that. And maybe a part of me is always going to want to be her friend. I know I fucked up, but I'm asking you to trust me, please. You're my one and only."

"I do trust you," Kara whispers, "that's what scares me. I would upturn the universe for you."

Lena's heart skips a beat, and she presses herself harder against Kara, moulding their bodies together until they are one. "I promise," she says in the crook of her neck, pressing her trembling lips to Kara's pulse point. "You hear me ? I love you and I promise you, you can trust me. Always."

She doesn't share her next thought, doesn't tell her how she too would ruin everything at her command, would find a way to crack the Earth in half with her bare hands if she needed her to ; some things are better left unsaid.

***

The next day is horrendous. If Lena had it her way, they wouldn't even leave the apartment, and would stay sheltered in their home, but they have, as she would put it if she weren't trying so hard to maintain composure, "shit to do."

Kara drops her off to work early, early enough that the streets below them are still mostly devoid of traffic and the morning air hasn't warmed yet, leaving her chilled despite the arms wound tight around her. Kara flies leisurely, taking her time in a way that Lena, who's gotten used to her top speed, isn't used to. It's enjoyable, peaceful, and for a moment, as they float above the city, she forgets all their troubles and what lies ahead of them. She's just free, and flying, and in love, and then Kara touches down on her balcony, and she's forced to confront reality.

Her office has been turned inside out by the cops, papers strewn around, and the picture of Kara and her that usually rests on her desk is on the floor amidst a splatter of broken glass. The computer, that she supposes Alex strong armed them into giving back, lays askew in a sea of unapproved patents and blueprints.

She steps inside hesitantly, her heels creaking on crushed glass and dirt from a fallen potted plant and goes straight to the shattered picture, picking it up to put it back in its rightful place. The frame is dented, and the glass covering fractured right in the middle, breaking the immortalised embrace.

"Do you want me to clean that up for you ?" Kara asks quietly, coming behind her to lay a gentle reassuring hand on her hip. "It'll take less than a minute."

"It's okay. I'll have a team come in as soon as I can get a hold of Eve."

She straightens her computer, feels around in the ocean of papers for her keyboard and boots the system, holding her breath until she hears the telltale sound of her hard drive waking up and the screen lights up with the first step of her decrypting protocol. It's cracked in the top right corner, but it's nothing that she can't fix.

"And have people rummage around you all day while you try to work ?"

"You make a good point," Lena mumbles, and it's all Kara needs to blur into action, leaving behind a trail of tidiness and a clean comforting smell. How the hell she found cleaning products this fast, Lena can only guess.

"But don't get cocky about it !" she calls out a second before Kara comes to a stop before her, a slight grin stretching her lips and not a hair our of place. She leans in to lay a quick soft kiss on her lips then takes a step back and straightens one last pile of files. Lena's office is as pristine as can be given the circumstances.

"I'm not cocky," Kara says, "I'm just that good."

"Don't be an asshole Supergirl," Lena says, rolling her eyes but smiling fondly nonetheless. Kara goofing around is exactly what she needs right now.

"Is that on the record Miss Luthor ?" Kara asks, holding out a pen as an improvised microphone.

"Yes it is," Lena replies, patting her arm patronisingly. "My reputation can't get much worse anyway."

"Lena..."

"Nothing but the truth."

Kara stares at her, frowning sadly.

"Alright," Lena concedes, throwing her hands in the air for the sake of drama, "no self-deprecation today."

"No self-deprecation at all, ever," Kara corrects, reaching out across the small gap that separates them to lay a hand on her cheek. Her palm is warm, and smells of Lena's hand cream.

"No self-deprecation today," Lena says, briefly turning to kiss Kara's hand. "That's my final offer."

Kara sighs, but she still draws her in for a hug. "You're terrible," she whispers, "but you're worth much much more than what they could ever think of you. You know that, right ?"

"I don't have to know, I always have you to remind me."

Kara's phone starts beeping and regretfully she takes a step back, smiling shyly when Lena closes the distance to straighten her crooked tie.

"You still need to try on your new suit. You can’t go around flying like that, you’ll ruin all your good shirts."

"Bring it home with you tonight ? I'll put on a show for you."

Lena feels her cheeks heat up at the suggestion and has to clear her throat before she can answer, croaking a little, "sure." Feeling like she has to even the playing field, she lifts herself slightly on her toe and kisses her on the corner of the mouth, leaving there a prominent red lipstick mark.

"Be careful today," Kara whispers, "no unnecessary danger, and if you need me-"

"I promise I won't do anything stupid," Lena cuts. "I’ll be careful."

"I'm a little scared," Kara breathes.

"I know." Lena smoothes the fabric of Kara's shirt, pressing hard against her shoulders as she does so. "But I won't let Lex get to you."

"I don’t want him to get to you," Kara replies, head hanging low. Her phone starts ringing again.

"He won’t. I won’t let him. Go now. That newspaper can't do anything without you."

Kara sighs, and after a final press of her lips to Lena's forehead, she dives out the window. She's back a couple of seconds later to drop Krypto off, the dog looking disheveled and absolutely offended. She doesn't linger, and her arrival to her own office is marked by a text, a stock image of two puppies hugging captioned "us."

The picture, rather inoffensive and very much Kara-like makes her heart ache. She turns her phone face down, and after a quick glance over her shoulder, logs into Lex's database. She might not let him get to her, but she will get to him.

***

Lena gets home early to the feeling that something is intensely wrong. The apartment is plunged in semi-darkness because they didn't bother opening the curtains this morning, but she doesn't need to turn on the lights to know something is amiss the moment she steps inside. Someone is in there with her, and the air feels different down to its molecules. It vibrates with the presence of the intruder in a way that rattles her to her core. The intruder does not move, but Lena knows they know she’s here. Krypto keeps quiet, frozen at her side, the memory of the kick he took to the head still too fresh in his mind for him to attack without being asked to.

As discreetly as she can, she feels around for the thick baseball bat they keep by the door ; a gift from Alex offered under the pretence of a joke but that she's very thankful to have right now, even if it won't offer her much protection if it's Lex. With her free hand, she flips de lights on quickly and has to refrain from taking a step back when she comes face to face with no other than, "Superman ?"

"Lena," the broad alien says in greeting, his voice stilled and lacking of any warmth. At the sight of him, Krypto starts growling.

She steels herself quickly, levelling him with a glare that only falls short of heat vision. "It’s Miss Luthor to you, Mister Kent," she says, "or better yet. Doctor Luthor." It really is time that people start acknowledging her numerous PhDs. She bends down to grab Krypto's collar and force him into a sitting position, ostensibly showing to the intruder that she's in control here. "Would you mind telling me why you’re invading my home ?"

He at least has the decency to look sheepish, but to Lena, it’s far from enough. "I though I would drop by," he says, crossing his arms behind his back, "to see Kara and um, discuss current events."

"Drop by uh ?" Lena repeats sarcastically. "A little less dropping by and a little more sticking around would have done wonders on her."

She’s got much more venom on her tongue, but before she can unleash the furry bubbling inside, Kara flies in through the window in a blur, landing between her and Superman with a strength that shakes the entire building.

She reaches behind to briefly squeeze her hand in a small gesture that says everything then refocuses all of her attention on the broad crushing silhouette of her cousin. "Kal," she says with a coldness that is becoming increasingly regular in her voice. "Was our last encounter not enough for you to understand I don’t want to see you again ?"

He doesn’t back down in front of her which to Lena is more insulting that anything he could have said. "We need to discuss the Luthor problem," he says, spitting Lena’s last name in a way that is all too familiar to her.

"No we don’t," Kara replies, ice cold. "We do not need to discuss anything at all and I do not need your input on anything. I can handle myself."

"This is important."

"You know what else is important Kal ?"

"I-"

"You know what else is important Kal ?" Kara repeats pointedly.

Shaking herself out of the premises of torpor, Lena takes a step closer to her, laying a discreet but comforting hand between her shoulder blades and pressing slightly as if to say "I’m here."

"What’s important Kal," Kara continues without giving him any time to answer, "is all the things you’ve never taken the time to say, all the other moments when you should have been there but never bothered showing up." Kara shakes with fury, and Lena presses harder against her back. "What about that time I died, and you didn’t show up to my funeral ? Or when I was hacked by the worse creature in the universe, and you couldn’t pick up your phone ?"

"I was light-"

"Light years away," Kara cuts bitterly, "I know. The thing is Kal, even when you’re here, your heart’s not in it. What about when my best friend took off with my niece and left my sister heartbroken and you knew how to track her down but didn’t say anything ? Or, and this is my favourite," Kara pauses to let out a strangled broken laugh, "when you abandoned me with strangers on an alien planet ? These are moments I would have needed you. You’ll notice today isn’t on the list. Get out."

"Kara..."

"I said get out Kal."

Superman hesitates a bit too long, and Lena can feel Kara is close to giving in to something that she will regret. Steeling herself, though she knows she must look absolutely ridiculous next to these two invulnerable beings, she rounds Kara and comes stand in between her and her cousin, twirling her bat around in what she wills to be a threatening gesture. Krypto follows, baring his teeth when he sits at her feet.

"I believe," she says, speaking slowly, "that Kara asked you to leave. I won't be as kind as her if I have to ask twice."

He hangs his head in defeat for a second then, sighing deeply, makes his way to the open window. "I'm sorry Kara," he says, "I really am. I know I haven't been the cousin you deserve, but I'm here now if you need help. I know Lex, I know how vicious he is and he will stop at nothing."

"I believe I'm the resident Luthor expert," Lena says, spitting her own name out in a perfect imitation of his previous tone. "We will be fine Mister Kent."

"Kara..." he tries again.

"Just go."

This time, he doesn't hesitate ; and quicker than Lena's eyes can follow, he's out of her sight. As soon as she registers his absence, she drops the bat, the metal clattering loudly on the ground, and turns to Kara, stumbling a little in her hast. She's standing very still, and if it weren't for the rise and fall of her chest, Lena would fear that she's been turned to marble. She smiles, her lips crooking a little at the corners, and before Lena can do anything, tears start streaming down her face.

15. The bough will break (Kara)

Summary for the Chapter:

In which Kara breaks down, Lena takes care of her and Alex comes to the rescue. Everyone needs a hug.

Notes for the Chapter:

Title is from Breakdown by Melissa Etheridge.

Kara isn't really sure why she's crying, just that the load of the past few days has suddenly become unbearable. She's doing her fucking best, and her fucking best isn't nearly enough.

Feeling that her legs won't support her much longer and afraid of causing an indent on the ground, or worse, of going straight through the floor, she lowers herself to a sitting position, resting her forehead on her knees. She's aware of Lena crouching down next to her, the bat loudly clattering on the ground in the process, and she can hear the vibration of her vocal cords, but can’t focus on the words she's saying. She perceives Krypto too, nuzzling her gently, his nose wet and cold against her skin, but absolutely cannot bring herself to care about it.

She would like to be able to move, thread her fingers through his short fur, reach out and take Lena's hand, but her body seems to be shutting down and she wonders if she's finally taken one too many hits and her insides are rusting and crumbling. It makes her feel strange, alien to her own body, and this in turn makes her panic.

She knows Brainiac is dead, she killed him herself, ripped him apart with her bare hands ; but sometimes, sometimes she can still feel him, in her head, sometimes she can feel his control coursing through her limbs, his robotic breath on the back of her neck. This feeling of not being herself, this remote awareness of her body, grips at her insides like a vice, and when she chokes on her next intake of air, it's like someone else has decided in her place that she shouldn't breathe. She notices her laboured breathing when the sensation of Lena's hand on her chest breaks through the numbness. She grasps at it, perhaps a little too roughly, and presses it hard against her. If she can do this, if she can reach out to Lena and take her hand, that means she's in control, that means she's here, and not locked inside of her head.

Somewhere close to her, something starts ringing, and comprehension of Lena's voice returns to her when she starts swearing frantically. She tries to focus on her words, but they're still hazy, and all she can deduce is that Alex is on the other side of the phone, worried about her once more. That's all she ever does anyway, causing people worry and heartache.

Lena hangs up, and asks her a question, her voice lifting at the end of an unheard sentence. She repeats it, then says a name, a name that Kara understands and latches on like a sailor to the last piece of a sinking ship.

"Alex is going to come check on you later, okay ? How about a bath first, and a cup of tea ?"

Kara nods. It's the best she can manage right now.

"Okay then," Lena says softly, "I'm going to draw you a bath. But you're gonna to have to help me if you want to get up." She chuckles sadly, and for some reason, the sound gets caught around Kara's heart. "You know I can't lift you on my own."

Kara nods again, and with little more warning shoots up to her feet, staggering in her lack of control. The world is a little fuzzy around the edges, but she does notice Lena taking a hasty step back. She expects to find fear on her face, but there's nothing there but a deep love and a nauseating care.

She follows her to the bathroom, hand loosely held in hers, and focuses on her heartbeat when the sound of the rushing water assaults her ears. She sits on the edge of the tub, lets Lena tenderly undo her tie for her and remove her shirt, her fingers nimble on the buttons. She slips her t-shirt and bra over her head, and it's to the feeling of her skin on her skin that Kara truly begins to return to herself.

She stands up to let Lena slide her trousers down, letting her bat her hands away when she tries to help, and steps out of the garment with minimum stumbling. "I'm fine," she manages to utter.

"No you're not," Lena says, pushing on her shoulders to sit her back on the ledge. "And that's perfectly okay. You've had a little bit too much to deal with lately and you're in shock. Just," she hesitates there, her voice slipping into a low plea, "don't lock yourself too deep inside your head, okay ?"

"Okay." Kara nods firmly. "Okay. Yeah." She presses a weary hand to her forehead, then rubs at her eyes and exhales loudly. "I'm sorry. I'm fine. Or I'll be in a minute."

Lena combs her hand through her hair, brushing away a couple of errand strands. Kara can't help but lean into the touch, closing her eyes for a second as she grounds herself in the motion. "Take your time."

"I should be better than that," Kara whispers before she can stop herself. "I'm Supergirl. I'm strong and infallible. I don't break down because of ridiculous abandonment issues."

"Darling, do you hear yourself ?" Lena pauses, no doubt expecting a reply, and when she doesn't get any, bends to check the temperature of the bath and turns off the tap. "You're not ridiculous," she continues, nudging Kara in direction of the water before she starts stripping off her own clothes. "And even Supergirl doesn't have to be strong all the time. You have people you can rely on. You have me. I know I'm not the most reliable person, but I'm here. Always."

Kara steps into the bath, the hot water kindly lapping at her skin. Before she can lower herself into it, Lena slips in behind her and gently guides her down until her back is pressed to her front in the reversal of their usual position.

"You've been through so much," Lena whispers, kissing her shoulder and wrapping her arms tight around her middle, "you're allowed to lose your shit once in a while."

And well, Lena is right, Kara has been through a lot ; and if someone is allowed to lose their cool, if someone is allowed to kick and thrash and scream, it's her. But she hates it. She's worked too hard, fought too much, to get where she is now, to be anything less than strong and reliable. And she knows it's stupid, though her therapist put it into more eloquent words, knows she's allowed to waver for a second ; but every time she does, every time she breaks down or wakes up screaming in the dead of the night, she's reminded of everything that rests on her shoulders that will collapse if she so much as bends. Too much is at stake, especially right now, for her to take a minute to sit down and cry.

Lena rubs comforting circles on her stomach and hums gently in her ear and bit by bit, Kara starts unwinding, the tension in her muscles slowly receding in favour of bone deep exhaustion. The water distorts her body, and she doesn't want to look at it, her skin still feeling itchy and strange, so she allows her eyes to close, and lets her head drop back on Lena's shoulder, sliding further into the warm bath. She could almost fall asleep right then and there but the thought of Lena left helpless to get her heavy body out of the tub keeps her awake. It also makes her laugh a little, a low chuckle scraping at her throat and sparking curiosity in Lena.

"What is it darling ?" she asks, kissing her shoulder again and squeezing her sides in the beginnings of a massage.

"Nothing," Kara replies. Then, "just thinking about you."

Lena chuckles too. "Well I'm glad you still find me funny."

A knock on the door interrupts whatever might have come next and Lena sighs. "I'll get it. That must be Alex."

Gently, she pushes on Kara's back, Kara going with the motion out of habit, until there's enough space for her to get out of the bath. She stands on the mat for a second, droplets of water dripping down her supple body, then reaches out for a fluffy bathrobe and wraps herself in it, dabbing at her face with the huge sleeves. It's a testament to how comfortable she feels around all of them now that she doesn't think twice before slipping out of the room to go open the door. Kara keeps a loose ear on the interaction, but she's recognised her sister’s heartbeat, and knows they're safe with her.

Krypto takes the opportunity of Lena leaving the door ajar to slip inside and he comes stand next to the tub, his head resting on the white acrylic ledge. Kara pats his head softly, trying to infuse reassurance in the motion to soothe the deep concern in his eyes. He cocks his head to the side, and she starts mumbling nonsense to him, confident that he understands at least some of the Kryptonese that tumbles from her mouth with aching familiarity.

She soaks in the water for a while longer, half tuned into the sounds coming from the other room ; the water boiling, a pack of biscuits being ripped open, a chair screeching on the floor, and through it all, Lena and Alex's concerned discussion about her. They worry about her, and Kara hates herself a little for causing them such grief ; she's done enough of that to last all of them for a lifetime. Not particularly ready to face them yet, she exits the bath nonetheless, patting herself dry before slipping into the bedroom to retrieve clean sweatpants and one of Lena's old college sweaters. She sits on the edge of the bed for a moment, feet drawing meaningless patterns on the carpet, until a knock sounds on the door and Alex's head appears in the crack.

"You're not avoiding me, are you ?" she asks, stepping inside after Kara vaguely acknowledges her presence with a nod.

Kara starts to stand up slowly, then sits back down with just as little speed when Alex settles on the bed.

"I'm not. I just needed a minute."

"Anything you want to talk about ?" Alex asks gently, absentmindedly playing with Krypto's ears after he lays his head on her lap. He sighs in contentment, closing his big puppy eyes.

"Not really. It's the same old story anyway."

"Kal was here," Alex prompts, and Kara sighs with much less happiness then her dog, knowing there's no way she's going to get out of here without giving in. "What did he want ?"

The question is most likely rhetorical, since Kara heard her sister ask it to Lena no longer than ten minutes ago. Still, she seethes, "stick his nose in my business I suppose. For the first time in his entire life."

"He shouldn't have done that," Alex comments, her voice weirdly low and strangled.

"Nooo," Kara says, her tone dripping with sarcasm, "you think ?"

She regrets it almost immediately when her sister sighs and squeezes her shoulder.

"I don't understand what would compel him to do that," Alex continues, "I mean, he's never really cared about you before."

"Thank you for this very astute observation."

"I'm sorry," Alex says, "this was very poorly worded."

"It was."

They lapse into a tense silence, one that sits uneasily between them. Kara isn't even mad at her sister ; or not specifically at her and more at the world in general. She feels a boiling furry mounting in her once again, one that her bath with Lena had managed to stave off.

"But you're right, "she says eventually, forcing her jaw open to let out words tinted by anger, "he never cared about me."

"I'm sorry. For the way he treated you. He's your family, and you deserve better than that."

"You're my family," Kara bites back.

"I am," Alex replies softly, "and I'm here for you always. If you need me to punch him in the dick, I will."

Kara lets out a strangled laugh, and when she glances at her sister, she finds her smiling sadly. Alex squeezes her shoulder again, then wraps her arm around her, coaxing Kara into leaning against her. The burning feeling in her chest abates a little.

"I'm serious !" Alex laughs, her body shaking in time with the strangely unhappy sound. "But you never needed him," she continues after a while, turning briefly to kiss the side of her head, "you know that, right ? You've always been stronger than him, better."

"I never needed him," Kara whispers because it's true, "but I wanted him here. I wanted him to want to be here for me." She bites back a sob, feeling angry again for her pesky tears. "And now, now that all this time has passed, now that I don't want him in my life anymore, he shows up all mighty and powerful to take care of my 'Luthor' problem."

Alex hums, and Krypto raises his head to look at her, curiosity picked by the sound. "I think he's scared," she says.

"I don't care that he's scared. I've been scared my whole life and I've made do without him."

"I'm not defending him, I'm trying to understand. Maybe he feels responsible or-"

"And I'm not responsible ?" Kara interrupts, perhaps a little too sharply. "I'm the one who oversaw the transfer ! What if I missed something ?"

"You didn't miss anything."

"You don't know that !" Kara shouts. "You're just like the rest of us ! You don't know what happened !" At the commotion, Lena rushes into the room, but now that she's started Kara can't stop screaming, even if she knows it will scare her. "And Lena went to jail ! Who knows what could have happened there !? He could have gotten to her ! She could be dead ! And I couldn't even help ! Because I'm not Andrea, and I can't pass through fucking walls ! I'm not fancy enough for that !"

Lena kneels before her, a hand tentatively resting on her knee, but it's Alex who speaks first, her words barely audible over Kara's laboured breathing. "What is this about Kara ? What's really bothering you ?"

She's too soft, too careful and understanding and Kara explodes. "I don't know," she whispers furiously, "I don't fucking know ! My head's messed up and I can't think and I-" She doesn't even finish her derailed train of thoughts, it hurts too much, like her brain is going to burst out of her skull, like she's going to cave in on herself, turning into a black hole that'll suck in everything she's ever loved.

"You're safe," Alex says, voice unnaturally steady, "you're safe here."

"That's not true." Kara's words border on a groan, and she's not sure anyone but her can understand them. "I've never been safe and you know it. First it was, it was," she swallows, gripping the side of her head forcefully to stop the pounding in her skull, then tears the name out of her throat, "Brainiac. Now it's Lex. I've never been safe, and if I go down, Alex if I go down, everyone goes down with me."

"I won't let that happen," Alex whispers.

"We won't let that happen," Lena echoes immediately, rising from her crouched position to sit on Kara's other side, her hand this time resting on her thigh. It's dangerous. They shouldn't be this close to her when Kara could definitely lose her cool at any moment, could snap and rip their hearts from their rib cages without missing a beat, like she's done before to countless people even if some will argue she wasn't herself at the time ; but she can't bring herself to push them away.

"We will fight for you until the very end," Alex continues, "you know that, right ? I'm never letting you go. And I know you're scared, I understand that. The world is going to absolute shit and we're all scared. But Kara, you are not alone."

"We're right here," Lena adds, "and we're not going anywhere."

Minute clarity returns to Kara, and with it, an embarrassing flow of tears.

"You don't have to be strong all the time," Alex says, rubbing a hand up and down her shaking back. "I promise you it's okay to break a little."

Kara wants to believe her so much that it hurts.

***

Alex ends up spending the night. They all settle on the couch to watch a movie Kara pays little attention to, her head on Lena's lap and her feet on Alex's, and when the clock strikes midnight and they decide to call it quits for the day, her sister simply remains there with a throw blanket and borrowed pillow.

The following morning, after Kara has been asked time and time again if she's okay to go to work, though she's decided to narrow her understanding of the question to the fact that she doesn't feel like she's going to scream anymore, Alex drops them both off in a DEO armoured van, leaving Kara with Krypto and an industrial size box of donuts. It won't take any less to get her through the day.

She bypasses three DEO agents in disguise on her way in and acknowledges their presence with a curt nod. For muscles mountains, they're relatively inconspicuous, dressed down respectively as a security agent, and two secretaries. Kara doesn't feel particularly reassured by their presence, she appreciates the effort put into hers and Lena's protection, but ultimately, they're nothing but more victims on the way to get to her.

The elevator bellhop, one of Cat's old fancy, is also a DEO agent and he breaks character to escort her to the stairs, eyes darting around in anguish. He's a newer recruit, less accustomed to being around her and as he ridiculously holds the door open for her, she can see his eyes dropping down to her biceps, no doubt comparing their size with his.

She makes her way up the stairs quickly, carrying Krypto so he doesn't lag behind, and after dropping a glazed donut on Nia's desk, makes her way to hers. It is, however, already occupied.

"Good morning, William."

Her greeting is a little forceful, but it has the merit of causing him to straighten up comically, the motion sending the coffee in his cup sloshing overboard and onto his lap. He hisses in pain and jumps up, desperately trying to pat his leg dry with a couple of napkins covered in pastry flakes. Kara has no intention of helping him, but the sight is too pathetic for her not to do anything.

"That looks painful," she says, extracting a clean handkerchief from her pocket and wiggling it in front of it. "You should ice this."

He grabs it, but doesn't thank her, and proceeds to attempt to clean his trousers. In Kara's humble fashion opinion, the stain is an improvement to the beige corduroy.

"Can I ask what you're doing at my desk ?" she asks with a hint of polite sarcasm when he finally abandons his fruitless endeavour.

"I need to talk to you," William replies in his usual boring drawl. "About the Luthors."

"And that involves snooping in my personal research ?" Kara gestures with her donut box, nearly hitting him in the process.

"I wasn't snooping !"

"That open file seems to indicate otherwise." She drops the box right on top of it, effectively obscuring her notes, then steps right into his space, Krypto crowding him on the other side. She knows she's being too aggressive, that this is exactly the type of behaviour that could get her in trouble, but she isn't in the mood to deal with William Dey. At all.

"I don't think you should be writing about the Luthors," he says, his stale coffee and cheap mints breath clogging her nostrils. "You're too entangled with this family to be objective."

"I'm not writing about the Luthors. I'm writing about L-Corp, one of today's top ranked companies with a focus on technology, which as such falls under the scope of the Tribune's, science section, which is me."

"Well you've been writing about L-Corp an awful lot."

He points to the newspaper poking out of Kara's satchel. It's been rolled in such a way that part of the title is visible. "LENA LUTHOR INNOCENT." Kara knows what the rest reads ; she's written it herself. "L-CORP CEO DISCUSSES STOCK-OPTIONS AND GETTING OUT OF LUTHOR CORP'S SHADOW." No one has to know she conducted that interview from Lena's bedside at the DEO.

She shrugs casually. "Well L-Corp has been involved in an awful lot of current events."

William's left eyebrow quiver. "Well at least let's pool our resources together then."

"Do you understand the meaning of the word no ?" Kara asks calmly. "I said no already. Your methods are dubious at best and if all you bring to the table is your own desire to get secrets out of a sick woman, then I refuse to enable you. If you've got a legitimate lead, pitch it to your editor. If not, drop it."

William remains still for a long minute, body shaking slightly from what Kara supposes is anger. He tries to stare her down, unsuccessfully, and when he finally looks away, his face contorts not in fury, but grief. Kara almost takes a step back at the strength of it, his suddenly overflowing sadness radiating from him in waves. Before she can make sense of it, or do anything at all, he walks away, almost tripping over Krypto in the process. His course indicates an intent of shoulder checking her but he seems to think better of it, a smart decision considering his fragile human body.

He doesn't walk far before he whirls around and exhales steadily. "Lex Luthor killed my best friend. All I want to know, is why."

"A lot of people died in the Metropolis bombings," Kara says, "for no other reason than he was mad."

She cringes at her own words, aware that she sounds a lot like she's dismissing his pain, but she doesn't know how else to tell him his best friend is just another number in Lex's body count.

"Russell didn't die in the Metropolis bombings. Luthor sought him out purposely, and when he left, there weren't enough body parts to piece him back together."

"Russell," the name rings a bell in Kara, "Rogers ?"

William nods. "If you'll excuse me now, I have work to do."

Kara can do little more than stand awkwardly as he walks away. She remembers Russell Rogers. Everybody remembers Russell Rogers. Detonated from the inside. They had to scrape the walls of his office to get enough DNA to identify his body. Lex never confessed to this during his trial, but the Luthor Corp components they found in what was left of the bomb were deemed enough proof.

***

The altercation leaves her deeply unsettled, and she spends the rest of the day gnawing on her donuts and researching Russell Rogers, Krypto dozing on her feet. She has a feeling the whole affair has been swept under the rug a little too quickly. She won't question Lex's involvement in this, but Russell's death seems too deliberate for him to be just another casualty on his warpath. But just like William, she gets stuck on the why ; especially since Rogers Engineering never was a true competitor to Luthor Corp. His company was dissolved immediately after his death, its name erased from the register and its assets sold for little profit. L-Corp apparently purchased most of them, and this is only the tip of the iceberg of Russell's entanglement with Lena's company. He was married, briefly, to none other than Andrea Rojas, his former assistant now works in L-Corp's R&D, and, after taking a deep dive on the internet, she even finds a picture of him and Jack Spheer caught in what Cat Grant would describe as a compromising position.

She emerges from her research a little after the time she usually goes home with not much to work on, or at least not enough to get William to back off from Lillian. She can understand his pain, and why he never quite managed to put this behind him, especially with Lex's recent resurgence in the news, but she can't let him ruin the fragile equilibrium between Lena and her mother ; or at least not until she knows for sure what happened to Russell Rogers.

She exits work via the balcony, soaring into the air with Krypto in her arms but sans her suit. She refuses to wear it until Lena's had the chance to see her in it and the goo that is still stuck in her old armour means that it creaks horrendously every time she moves. She'll get around cleaning it eventually ; once someone invents military grade goo remover. She does a loop-the-loop, to Krypto's great dismay, and laughs brightly at the thought of Alex's face if it were to be named "Goo Gone."

She lands directly on the roof where Lena already is, nursing a cup of tea and gaze lost far off into the distance. "You're home early," she says as she settles on the ledge next to her and presses a sweet kiss to her temple. She's already changed into loungewear, leggings, thick fuzzy socks and one of Kara's old t-shirts, and her hair smells of her shampoo and faintly of hot plastic.

Lena hums quietly, then, after she's rearranged herself to both lean against her and press her hand on Krypto's head, says ; "board meeting was boring me to death so I dismissed everyone and went home. What's good being the boss if I can't just do what I want ?"

Kara laughs at that. "I suppose you're not wrong."

"Oh I know I'm right. But I'm exhausted. I've done everything I could except for swinging a hammer at the stock market to fix it and everyone will get a hefty bonus for Christmas. What more do they want ?"

"Something to complain about I suppose. That's what Cat used to say about CatCo's board."

"Ever the wise woman," Lena says, threading her fingers with Kara and waving them around aimlessly in the air. Beyond their dancing hands, the street lights start turning on. "Will she be in town soon ? I was thinking about inviting her to brunch. Unless she's more of a dinner person. Speaking about dinner, do you want pizza ?"

"I always want pizza," Kara answers, laughing, "and I'll ask Cat when she's thinking about visiting. I can probably bribe her with a private tour of my exhibition and some tales of Krypton for my official biography."

"Your official biography ?" Lena repeats, halfway between surprise and amusement. "Isn't that a little presumptuous ?"

"Didn't I tell you about that ? Cat called dibs on writing my tragic life story."

"Of course she did."

Kara doesn't need to look at her to know she's rolling her eyes in mockery but she does anyway, getting lost momentarily in Lena's amusement, the gracious smile on her lips, her eyes crinkling at the corner.

"What ?" Lena asks when she catches her watching.

"Nothing. I just love you a lot."

"I know," Lena whispers, "I'm very lucky."

She begins to lean in, her heart rocketing in anticipation. But behind this revered sound, Kara hears something else, something that causes her to pause before her lips can touch Lena's. Something crackles softly, inaudible probably to anyone that isn't her. It's not this that worries her though, she's used to hearing electricity coursing around and in her, but the distinctive ticking noise that accompanies it.

Lena opens her eyes, frowning, but Kara stops her question before she can ask it by raising a hand slowly. She coaxes her head to the side, tracking the noise back to its source down in the basement. It could be nothing, it probably is nothing ; but these days, she can never be too sure of things.

She listens hard. The screeching noise gets louder and louder, faster too, like whatever is emitting it is getting ready to go off.

The ticking stops.

Kara counts nine people in the building right now, not including the both of them, and she knows she won't have the time to get them all out before the bomb goes off.

Notes for the Chapter:

Life's been a bit shit lately so I hope you're all being kind to yourselves.

16. With you I’m always home (Lena)

Summary for the Chapter:

In which Kara cannot save everyone, we say goodbye to a key landmark of Dreamboat and Kara and Lena finally get the break they deserve but in less than ideal circumstances.

Notes for the Chapter:

Title from Always home by Selah Sue.

Fair warning that if, like me, you are irrationally attached to material possessions, this chapter might be a bit upsetting.

It takes a second for Lena to catch up. She was just leaning towards Kara, fully intending on kissing her and maybe getting a bit of semi-public pre-dinner activity ; and now she's in the street below, ears ringing from an explosion, and the entire building is tipping forward ready to lay down on its flank, right where she's standing.

Kara zooms in and out of the building, a blur of blue and red, and the other residents blink into existence next to Lena, startled, afraid, but alive. The kids are crying. They must be if the way their faces are contorting is anything to go by, but all Lena can hear is a grating high pitched noise that makes her want to vomit. She needs to get a grip on herself, return to her senses and shepherd everyone out of the way of the falling building but instead she finds herself hunched forward, bile dribbling out of her mouth.

A sharp and short scream resonates from inside the building and a moment later, the entire first floor disappears, reduced to rubble between ground level and the rest of the structure. The distressed noise pierces through the veil clouding Lena's senses and she shakes herself up, wiping her mouth on the back of her hand. The building is still tilting precariously, casting the survivors into its shadow.

"We need to get away from here," she croaks, her voice too low to be fully audible.

No sooner has she spoken that the building accelerates its course downward, and no one in its path is making any move to escape it. They all stand there, frozen in the face of impending doom, Lena included. Krypto is whimpering and pulling on her sleeve, teeth sinking into the soft fabric but even his urgency is not enough to get her to react beyond a few words. She knew it was going to happen, that it was only a matter of time ; but she still wasn’t ready for disaster to strike again so soon.

Glass breaks, raining down on them as furniture starts pushing through the windows, precipitated forward by the sharper angle of the building. A plate, painted with lovely pink flowers and a gold trim, explodes right at Lena's feet. A second blast shakes everyone to the ground and a blink of an eye later, a geyser of flames shoots through the building. That, she thinks idly, must be the faulty gas conduct they voted to get fixed at the last assembly. She's proven right when a moment later, the ground floors of both adjacent buildings light ablaze.

In the distance, sirens, all around her, screams of fear and pain ; in her head, Lex's maniacal laughter.

Kara reappears, a limp figure held tight in her arms. She hovers in the air for a moment, face darkened by the smoke and body shaking from exertion, then, back first, her muscled shoulders colliding harshly with the brick wall, she takes the brunt of the falling building and attempts to slow its course down. This, clearly, doesn't have the desired effect and part of the building seems to fold in on Kara, falling faster and faster before the top collides with the one opposite the street with a thunder-like sound and everything becomes eerily still.

Lena's chest rises and falls rapidly, and it's the only thing she can concentrate on right now as the ashes settle around her. Kara lands at her feet, cracks spreading from her like spider web on the pavement, and gently, she lays down the figure in her arms. It's Mrs Meyer. Or whatever is left of her ; her face charred, her limbs crushed, and her blush pink bathrobe now a sickening blood red.

"I," Kara stammers. "She. I couldn't get to her in time."

There's blood on her gloved hands, and on her ashen face ; and a piece of flesh that isn't her own as gotten stuck to her torso. She looks frail all of sudden, not much like the giant she is, and she looks about ready to fall to her knees, lips already parted in the beginning of a heartbreaking wail, when a screeching sound causes all of them to look up to witness their building slowly continuing its descent, taking down the one opposite in the process.

Fuck Lex. Really.

More screams rise, coming now from all sides of the street as inhabitants begin to spill out of their own buildings. They need to act, and they need to act fast. But before Lena can reprise her role of maladjusted shepherd and get everyone away from certain death, a gust of glacial wind and a black blur cross the street at incredible speed. Sam skids to a stop in front of her, slipping on a patch of newly created ice, and readjusts her hood to hide her face. "Okay," she mumbles to herself, "okay, a little strong on the freeze breath, but not bad."

"A little strong," might be too much of a euphemism, the entire street is covered in ice. At least, the nascent fires are extinguished. Kara draws herself to her full height, finally averting her eyes from Mrs Meyer's limp body.

"Alex and the DEO are on the way," Sam continues, to them this time. "The two of you need to get out of here. Do you know where the car is parked ?"

"The car ?"

"Yes," Sam replies with urgency. "Your getaway car. To get to the safe house. Lena please, now is not the time to freeze."

"The keys are in my satchel," Kara whispers, looking around like she's surprised she doesn't have her bag with her, "up there," she then adds, pointing at the roof of their building that now stands several storeys lower and at a dangerous angle. "But I can’t leave now, people need Supergirl."

"Lex Luthor tried to kill you ! Again !" Sam shouts. "You can't stay here !"

"I don't think he tried to kill us."

Sam whirls around to look at Lena again with furious astonishment. "You don’t what ?"

"Look at the way the building collapsed. He wanted to give us enough time to get out."

Loud screams derail the train of Lena's thought, and before she can assess the situation, she finds herself sprawled on her ass a couple of feet away from where Kara now stands with a piece of collapsed railing on her shoulders. The hero stares at the piece of metal for a moment, looking almost bewildered by its existence which, Lena supposes, is an appropriate reaction to having something crash on you, invulnerable or not.

Then, like the proverbial light bulb just came alive above her head, she shoots up from the ground, starts tearing the railing of all the windows, and with a little help from heat vision, solders them between the two buildings to stop the imminent collapse. The awful creaking finally stops and Lena can finally hear in the distance loud sirens and the screeching of tires.

"Good thinking," Sam says when Kara lands back down, "but you need to get out of here now, you've lingered long enough."

She's barely done talking that Kara has disappeared again, wafting in and out of the closest buildings to get people out in the street and away from immediate danger. She slows down her speed to something humanly manageable, no need to have everyone barfing over each other from superspeed, and the sight twinges at Lena's heart, especially when she shoots back in to get a family cat and a teddy bear. This, the person who went back inside a near-collapsed building to rescue of little kid's plushy, is who her brother wants to kill.

She briefly lands next to them again but flies up before Sam can open her mouth and returns with two backpacks filled to the brim, a crooked cardboard box and their respective laptops.

"I couldn't get everything in one go," she says sheepishly, toying with the handle of Lena's briefcase.

"It's okay I-" Lena starts, suddenly very aware that this isn't okay at all.

"I'll recover whatever I can get from your place and keep it safe for you, okay ? I promise." Lena nods at Sam’s words, looking up at her apartment. She isn't sure much is salvageable from it. "Now you get in the car, and you drive, and you don't stop, and when you get to the house you don't come out until Alex tells you it's safe. Okay ? Alex and no one else."

Sam briefly clasps Kara’s shoulder, then draws Lena in for a tight hug and when she lets go, pushes her in the general direction of the car. She breaks into a clumsy run, staggering until Kara scoops her from the ground and dashes to their vehicle. The DEO storms the street right when they get to it, car doors flying open and loud voices attempting to bring a semblance of order to the scared and recently homeless crowd. For a strange infinite second, Lena can feel Alex's hawk-like gaze on her through the SUV tinted window ; then the engine roars to life, and the car peels off the pavement.

***

They drive for a long time ; long enough that Lena would have normally fallen asleep by the time Kara finally slows down on the very edge of National City's suburbs. She turns in the last street before the desert, the vast stretch of sand disappearing beyond what her eyes can see. Most of the houses look worn and unsafe, and the street lights flicker ominously as they drive by. Lena can't possibly fathom how they'll be safe here.

The car comes to a stop in front of the most decrepit of houses, the structure closer to a ruin than actual shelter, and Lena is starting to wonder how something that looks like it has carpeted mouldy walls could be a safe place in any sense of the term when Kara stops in front of the house and a thin translucent barrier flutters in Lena's sightline. Kara leans over the dashboard, enters a quick command and only after that turns in the driveway, a loud pop welcoming Lena to an almost completely soundless world on the other side of what might have once been a prime and proper white picket fence.

Kara exhales slowly. "I knew I could trust Alex. We’ll be safe here."

It's the first words she's spoken since they got into the car.

"Great," Lena mumbles to herself, sarcasm dripping from her low voice, "the other collapsing building didn't get us, but this one surely will."

"Alex wouldn't send us there if it weren't 100% safe," Kara says, slamming the trunk of the car vigorously.

"I know. I'm sorry. I just-"

"You've had a long day," Kara interrupts softly before Lena can fully descend into frustration. "It's okay, I understand."

I’ve had a long life, is the reply on the tip of Lena's tongue, but instead of voicing it, she snatches the keys from Kara's outstretched hand, and stalks inside the house.

The house is less decrepit on the inside than it appeared to be on the outside. The walls are still carpeted, in a swirling pattern of mauve and plum, but the abomination doesn't extend to the creaking floorboards, and a strong scent of citrusy cleaning products thankfully permeate the air. The windows don't open, but thanks to the shield protecting the house, they'll at least be able to take a breather on the front porch.

Yellow light floods the living room from an antiquated chandelier, casting everything in unsettling shadows. Lena does a quick check of the house, poking her head in the kitchen to take notice of a very dangerous looking gas stove. There's not even a microwave and in fact, the only somewhat modern piece of equipment seems to be a pistachio plastic corded telephone glued to the wall in the entryway. When Lena picks it up, it doesn't emit a tone. Upstairs, a crooked corridor leads to a single bedroom, in which the sheets don't appear to have been woven in this century, and a bathroom with an old bathtub and an overhanging shower head that has been tentatively cleaned with what smells like white vinegar.

The water pressure is terrible, and the temperature knows no in between between scalding and freezing but she still welcomes it with tears of relief. She lathers herself with the soap Kara speedily packed for her and relishes in the familiar clean smell that, for a second, tricks her mind into thinking she's okay. She feels like she hasn't breathed properly since her building collapsed, and it's probably true. She tilts her head back under the thin stream and closes her eyes, opens them again immediately when the semi darkness of her closed eyelids brings about the bloody image of Mrs Meyer's corpse. She'll never get to see the progress Lena made in her robotic help for seniors program.

With no access to the outside world, there's no way of knowing if she was the sole victim of the collapse, but whatever the final death toll, Kara is sure to be beating herself up about it downstairs. Regretfully, Lena turns off the water, and after towelling herself dry slips on a pair of sweatpants and one of the two hoodies Kara grabbed from the wreckage, she pads her way downstairs, her socks almost sending her to an early grave when she slips in the slanted staircase.

She finds Kara in the kitchen, engrossed in the back of a pack of ramen as she tries to make sense of the tiny writing. From afar, Lena can see it's old, probably dating back from before harmful additives were banned from processed food, but she's ravenous enough not to care. She frowns adorably at the packet, and when she notices Lena's presence and raises her head to look at her, a grim smile stretches sadly on her face.

"How's the shower ?" she asks, nearly hitting Lena in the head with the ramen pack when she wiggles in between her arms for a hug.

"Terrible."

Kara sighs. "If I fly out very quickly, I can get a hold of Alex and have us move somewhere better."

Lena's chest warms a little at the proposition and she looks up at Kara, at this woman she loves so much and who would ruin everything for her. "No," she says with not an ounce of regret. "They're right. Alex, Sam, all of them. We need to stay put until the DEO has done its job. I won't risk you for poor water pressure." She kisses the bottom of her jaw, the only place she can reach since Kara is still in her suit and her shock absorbing boots give her a nice height advantage. "I promise you I'll be fine. It'll be like a holiday."

"In the shittiest house in the history of houses."

"Reminds me of a guest house I stayed at in England actually," Lena muses, "carpeted walls are very British."

"What's up with that anyway ?" Kara laughs, "it's giving me the creeps."

"No idea. But you get used to it, it's homely."

"I'll keep that in mind for our future ho-."

Kara stops abruptly, but the damage is done, and she sags in on herself, the brunt of her weight suddenly resting on Lena who staggers a little in surprise. She straightens up just as quickly as she deflated, but doesn't carry herself with the same strength.

"I'm going to go," she points at the ceiling, "take a shower. Don't wait for me if you're hungry."

"I'm sorry," Lena says as Kara retreats through the door, "about Lex."

"It's not your fault. I'm the one who didn't want to move out."

There are many other words on the tip of Lena's tongue, but before she can string any of them together, Kara has disappeared upstairs, and the water pipes start creaking menacingly. Shaking herself up, Lena wipes an angry tear before it can fully spill, then sets to boiling some water in a dented pan. She doesn't know how much more they can carry before they definitely break.

Kara stays in the bathroom for a long time, the shower running only for a short portion of it. Lena considers joining her for a second, just to forget for a moment all the fuckery happening around them. In the end, she doesn't, and instead sets to preparing dinner, finding in a cupboard a stash of protein bars that might be Kara's only chance to keep up her high calorie intake. She sniffs one by curiosity and has to fight back the urge to vomit ; protein bars are not exactly a choice meal, especially when the chocolate covering has gone grey and stale. She sets a handful aside with two packs of ramen and what was once a brand new bottle of Tabasco ; with a bit of luck, it hasn't gone bad yet and will revive the rest of their food.

None of this bodes well with her. She can see how this place would be part of the DEO's arsenal, strangers things have happened with that organisation, but she doesn't understand why Alex would agree to send her sister to a place like this, with too little food to sustain her, and a security system less complex than what Lena came up with on a regular basis in her teenage years.

While she mules over this, she brews herself a strong cup of tea, the only thing that isn't in short supply here. She finds ten bright red boxes of her favourite brand, still wrapped, and an unused electric kettle, free of any limestone, that immediately beats the corded phone for most recent working device in the house. Kara did pack her phone and tablet, but the house's security system is jamming them and they’re unusable. She tries not to think about it too much, about the way they're effectively cut off from everything, but the cellphone she's slipped in her pocket out of habit is heavy, and refuses to be forgotten.

When Kara finally gets out of the bathroom, they eat dinner in companionable silence, legs tangled under the table. Dinner in the broad sense of the term, their meal qualifies more as a mid night snack and by the time they're done and Kara declares that she will do the dishes in the morning, dawn is already peaking through the hastily closed curtains. They go to bed with some hesitancy, both afraid that they won't be able to sleep ; but the sheets have a nice comforting lemony smell that Lena can't place and despite herself, she quickly succumbs to slumber in Kara's tense arms.

***

/Lena can't get the acrid smell out of her nose ; she's convinced that the deflagration charred her sensitive nostrils. She would have sworn the capacitor was soldered on properly when she checked but clearly, it wasn't. If Lex hadn't been here, well, she'd be in a much worse state than a burnt palm and a new haircut. Her pride really is much more wounded than she is. How could she be so careless in her work ?

A soft knock on her door drags her out of her impromptu pity party and Lex pokes his head in without waiting for an answer. His receding hairline is really starting to show, even with the impressive amount of gel he's used to arrange his hair.

"Can I come in ?" he asks though he's already inside. "I brought some tea."

Lena sighs, then nods, and it's enough of an invitation for him to come sit on the bed next to her on top of the heavy comforter.

"It's Barry's," he says when she takes a sip out of her mug.

She presses the tea to her chest, letting the warmth seep inside of her, and mumbles her thank yous.

"Everybody makes mistakes Lena," Lex continues, tenderly brushing away a strand of her shortened hair. "Failure is a part of invention, it's how you deal with it that matters."
"I know," Lena whispers.

"And how are you going to deal with this mistake ?"

"Sleep on it. Work twice as hard tomorrow."

Lex smiles, ruffles her hair gently. "Excellent."

Lena leans against her brother's shoulder, taking in the clean zesty scent of his suit that breaks through the stench of smoke in her nose, and wonders where she would be without him./

The first few days pass by in a strange manner. There's not much to do around the house, and Kara spends an inordinate amount of time sitting by the phone, waiting for Alex to call. She blames herself, that much is clear, and being cut from the outside, not knowing how many people made it out, how many died, doesn't help. She stares at her hands often, clenching and unclenching them nervously. There's still blood under her fingernails that hasn't been completely washed out. After conducting a deep inspection of the house, Lena finds a couple of battered old books, romance mostly, and decades old science journal, as well as an old record player with a single Chet Baker vinyl.

She spends the major part of these first few days sitting with Kara, reading, sometimes aloud to distract the both of them. It's better than colour coding the meagre pantry to make up for her new and terrifying lack of routine. She wishes she could do more, or anything at all really, but she finds herself stuck, rooted in place on the other side of the rift Kara is attempting to dig between them. She can't really hold it against her, she understands why Kara is reacting the way she is, she simply wishes it weren't so. After the first day, where they slept so well, the nights aren't so kind anymore, and Lena seldom sleeps through them, more often than not lying awake and cursing Lex for what he did. Cursing herself too for what she let him do to them.

She finds a modicum of hope and solace in the little things, in the way Kara will sometimes drape most of her body weight around her while she's cooking, or slip in the shower with her in the morning. In the fact that she still holds her at night, and always, always leaves room for her to sit next to her by the phone, or on the porch when she steps out for fresh air. This is how she knows not all is lost, how she knows Kara is trying, and she can keep on trying too.

"I'm sorry," Kara finally says one evening as they're eating in the relative silence of cutlery scraping on plates. "I know I'm scaring you and I know it doesn't look like it but I'm really trying not to."

Lena sets her fork down delicately. "I understand," she says, "it's hard not to shut someone out." She means no harm by this, but Kara still winces at the reminiscence of recent days. "Do you want to try and talk about it ?" she asks, as gently as she can manage.

She's gotten used to Kara's prolonged bout of silence, though they've been happening less often the further away they've gotten from her return to life and Earth ; she most often gets out of them on her own, but this time, maybe she needs a little coaxing.

"I can't stop thinking about them," Kara whispers eventually after another stretch of silence. "I just can't. All these people they've-"

She stops, twirls her noodles on her fork angrily. Lena reaches out slowly, taking her hand in hers to stop the carnage before the ceiling accidentally gets painted a new unfashionable colour.

"They've lost their homes because of me. Nothing I can do will ever fix that."

So, here's the root of her current round of anguish. Lena's heart breaks a little at the realisation. Kara's relationship with home as a concept has always been fraught ; she's lost hers so young, and to such a web of lies and trauma, and she's been clinging to the every place she's lived in with something not unlike desperation ever since. It's only natural, now that Lena thinks about it, that she would react so viscerally to her failure to keep her neighbour's homes safe ; but it's not her fault, or not solely, and Lena doesn't know how to explain that without starting a fight.

"I should have known better," Kara continues, seething, "than to think we were safe. I should have trusted Kal, and I should have listened to Alex, and I could have, I could have wrapped myself around the bomb or-"

"Should haves aren't going to get us anywhere," Lena interrupts gently. "There are a lot of things I should have done differently too. And Alex no doubt thinks the same, J'onn too probably, hell, President Marsdin is probably up to her neck in 'should haves'. But looking back isn't going to do us any good right now, we can only look forward and do our best. And we can't let Lex break us." Lena barely breathes, carried away by her own words. "I can survive a lot of things, but I wouldn't survive losing you because of him, and if we let his scheming and bullshit get in between us, that's exactly what's going to happen. My home is not a place, it's a person and that person is you. I'll let him take everything away, I'll give it up without a fight if I must, but not you. Never you."

She stops. Feels strangely compelled to shovel noodles into her mouth to prevent herself from going on another grandiloquent rant ; but Kara smiles at her sadly from the other side of the table and she puts her fork back down.

"You're right," Kara whispers, "I can't let him win." Her brow furrows, and she looks down at the content of her plate with intent, like it holds some kind of prophecy. "If you're okay, here, with me," she continues eventually, "even though we don't have a home anymore, do you think all these people are too ?"

"What do you think about when you think of home ?"

"You," Kara replies without missing a beat. "Alex, Krypto, the sound of his tail on the floor when he's happy, Eliza, her hugs and cookies, Sam, and playing cards with Ruby and- Oh."

"There it is. You've got your answer," Lena says, feeling wiser than she really is. "They'll be upset. I know I am. I know I'll miss our apartment, and our roof, and the way the sun crossed the room. But they're alive, and together, all thanks to you. Ultimately, that's what matters."

Kara rubs a weary hand on her face. "You're right."

"I know I am. It's exhausting."

Kara laughs, just a little but enough for Lena to know her quip fulfilled its intended purpose. She glances at the phone in the hallway, doesn't say anything, but her silent question is deafening anyway. When is Alex going to call ?

17. You’re the only place I know (Kara)

Summary for the Chapter:

In which Kara and Lena find tenuous peace but shit goes down rather quickly.

Notes for the Chapter:

Haven't looked at this story in a while because I'm working on other stuff (😏) but I was happy to spend some time with it again and I hope you like this chapter.

Title is from the same song as previous chapter but I did add Almost Blue by Chet Baker which is playing at the beginning of the chapter when Kara and Lena are dancing.

Kara is very adaptable. Ultimately, it's the biggest tragedy of her life. She goes with the flow, her head never underwater for too long ; and no matter how hard the punches, no matter how deep the grief, she always rises again, her pain relegated to a little part of her heart. If there's one thing however that she never quite adapted too, it's the noise levels on Earth. Her hearing is always the first to give out when she panics, the first to awake when she rises from sleep. Here though, what bothers her is not the noise, but the absence of it. Apart from the light buzz of electricity that she tuned out quickly, it's eerily quiet behind the forcefield. There are no birds, no car horns, no hundred of thousands of heartbeats, it's just her, and Lena, and it's unnerving. She can't periodically check for danger, can't see if anyone is coming, and most of all, she can't hear Alex. She could get used to the rest, just peace and quiet and Lena ; but not hearing her sister, not knowing if she's okay and safe might be what tips her over the edge.

She looks down at her hands, covered in soapy water, and with a sigh, slowly straightens the fork she's just bent in two. A set of feet pads closer behind her and soon, two arms wrap around her, hands coming together just below her chest. Lena's head pops up over her shoulder ; she smells of toothpaste, and the clean citrusy smell that permeates everything here.

"What kind of atrocious book do you want to read tonight ?"

Kara mulls over it for a second, then puts the scrubbing brush down in the sink and swiftly turns around in Lena's arms. "Do you have anything about lesbians in lockdown ? Post-apocalyptic bunker romance ?"

She means it as a joke, but her tone is a little too acerb for it to land right. Thankfully, Lena laughs anyway, a graceful chuckle reverberating in her throat. She kisses her cheek, close to the mouth. "I'll see what I can find," she says. "Don't wash the dishes too hard, okay ?"

Kara makes no such promise.

Music starts crackling out of the living room ; Lena must have put on their sole record. Luckily, it's not one Kara dislikes, though jazz now always reminds her of her final hours at Luthor manor before Brainiac attacked. Definitely abandoning the dishes, she makes her way to the other room silently and finds Lena gently swaying in front of the almost barren bookshelf, engrossed in a back cover.

"Found anything good ?" she asks, matching the sway of Lena's hips with her own as she gently encases her waist between her hands.

"No." Lena puts the book back on the shelf. "This one is about straight people shagging in a lighthouse. Not really my thing."

Kara moulds her body against her back, kisses the crown of her head. In the background, Chet Baker starts crooning ; it's not a happy song. "What ?" she asks, "lighthouses or straight people ?"

"Ha ha, very funny."

"You don't sound amused," Kara muses.

"You think ?"

Even if she’s turning her back to her, Kara can perceive Lena's patented eyebrow raise. "Shame," she says, twirling her until they're face to face, "I was thinking of writing you a romance novel."

Lena wraps her arms around her neck, smoothing her fingers on the shorn hair at the base of her head. "Humour me then."

"It's about this alien," Kara begins, "who's been on Earth for a while. She's doing good in life, she has a job, a family, but she's also very lonely. One day, as she's coming home, she stumbles, quite literally, on the most beautiful woman she's ever seen, in the whole universe."

"In the whole universe," Lena repeats, "of course."

"Don't interrupt me," Kara scolds lightly, briefly squeezing her waist, "it's a very good story. It has robots, and dogs, an epic battle between good and evil."

Lena smirks. "Sounds more like an action movie."

"Tons of sex," Kara continues, "like loads and loads of it. And sweet kisses and dates too, hand-holding-"

"The hand holding is very important," Lena comments with a laugh. She shudders when Kara slips her hands under her shirt.

"The hand holding is very important."

"How does it end ?"

"It doesn't," Kara replies softly.

"I think this is my favourite part."

"It's mine too."

Slowly, with intent, she leans in to kiss her, and Lena meets her in kind, mouth already open and welcoming, lips hot and eager. At once, nothing else matters. Not the record skipping loudly between two songs, not the fact that she can't hear anything beyond the forcefield ; she's not even afraid anymore. All there is, all she cares about, is Lena, her warm body pressed against hers, her feather light weight when she lifts her up by her thighs to carry her up to bed. There will be time later to finish doing the dishes, to fix the record player, to worry about a thousand big and little things ; right now, all Kara wants to focus on is Lena's pale skin against the dark sheet, her laugh when she gets caught in her sweater, the trail blooming down her lithe body, the blood rushing loud on either side of her head, when she wraps her legs tight around her.

***

The next couple of days are strange. They pass by slowly, Kara trying her best not to worry too much while Lena grows incredibly nervous the more time they spend cooped inside. She's adapted too, and relatively well considering the situation, but it's not rare for Kara to walk into a room to find her obsessively straightening small objects while counting over and over under her breath. She also touches the wall next to the phone every time she walks past it then wipes her finger on her slacks. Kara doesn't think Lena's noticed she does that.

Kara packed her things, that's the main reason why she returned to their wrecked apartment, but she seems afraid of unpacking them, and they stay neatly arranged in their cardboard box, the frame around her birth mother's picture dented and the glass of Ruby's snowball cracked in several places. She's put small pieces of tape on it to avoid the sparkly liquid from seeping out but she'll have to find a more permanent solution soon. Somehow, this feels like a very shitty metaphor for the current state of their lives.

"Who do you think is taking care of Krypto ?" Lena asks late one afternoon, a bit too casually. She's been working on Kara's code for the past hour, trying to find a way to up her tolerance to Kryptonite, and she lifts her head from her tablet to ask her question, pushing her glasses up to adjust them on her nose. Kara forgot to grab the contact lenses cleaning solution.

"Alex probably. We might have some trouble getting him back from her."

"I'll buy her a dozen puppies," Lena grumbles, rather cutely, "but she's not keeping my dog." She puts her tablet down, presses her fingers hard on her forehead. "Sorry, I think I've hit a wall there. It'd be better if I could look directly inside you, but I don't have the right cable."

"You should make me wireless," Kara says, rubbing at the base of her neck where the scar never truly faded.

"If there's one thing we are absolutely not going to do, it's that," Lena says very firmly. "We can't risk every idiot with a cellphone and too much free time hacking you."

"I didn't think of this," Kara mumbles, properly chastised and feeling a bit like a four years old caught with her hand in the cookie jar.

"It's okay," Lena replies, gently kissing her cheek. "I can think about it for you."

Kara hums, rubbing at her neck again. "With your cute genius brain."

"Well my 'cute' genius brain is tired," Lena huffs, "I think I'm done for today."

A shadow passes over her face and for a second, she looks particularly upset, brow set into a heavy frown, before she smoothes her features and gets up from the couch, as proper as can be in her crinkly clothes.

"Do you want to get dinner on the roof ?" Kara asks, following after her immediately.

"On the roof ?"

"Yeah." Kara looks down at her feet, rubbing at the collar of her t-shirt. She found it in one of the closets and took it upon herself to cut off the tag but did so improperly and now it's itchy. Alex always cuts the tag of her clothes for her, having grown expert at it, but Kara supposes she had other things to worry about when she set up everything ; her sister might not have even been the one who took care of the safe house.

"I know it's not the same," she continues hesitantly, "but it could be nice. I'll make sure you don't fall."

Lena considers it for a second, then, leaning into Kara's arms, simply says, "okay."

"Okay ?"

"Yeah," she breathes. "It'll be nice. So far out of town, we'll see the stars better."

Getting out onto the roof as it turns out, is slightly more complicated than Kara had envisioned. It's steep for starters, and the tiles are rough and cutting, eliciting a good number of curses from Lena. Kara does offer to help, but her girlfriend seems to be in the mood to do things on her own, and in any case, her hands are busy juggling their noodles and an old bottle of wine unearthed from beneath the sink.
